translations.literal: ○ Song Cheng, Xue Lu
translations.idiomatic: Song Cheng and Xue Lu

sentences.zh: （郭義金玉）

translations.literal: (Guo Yi, Jin Yu)
translations.idiomatic: (Guo Yi, Jin Yu)

translations.literal: Liu Rong, Zhu Rong, Fei Huan, Tan Guang, Chen Huai
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong, Zhu Rong, Fei Huan, Tan Guang, and Chen Huai

translations.literal: (Ma Liang)
translations.idiomatic: (Ma Liang)

translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gui

translations.idiomatic: (Sun Wan)

sentences.zh: 任禮趙安趙輔劉聚宋晟，字景陽，定遠人。

translations.literal: Ren Li, Zhao An, Zhao Fu, Liu Ju. Song Cheng, styled Jingyang, was a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li, Zhao An, Zhao Fu, and Liu Ju. Song Cheng, styled Jingyang, was a native of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父朝用，兄國興，並從渡江，皆積功至元帥。

translations.literal: His father Chaoyong and elder brother Guoxing both followed in crossing the Yangtze, both accumulating merit until reaching commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chaoyong and elder brother Guoxing both followed in the crossing of the Yangtze and, through accumulated merit, rose to the rank of commander.

sentences.zh: 攻集慶，國興戰歿，晟嗣其職。

translations.literal: Attacking Jiqing, Guoxing died in battle; Cheng succeeded to his post.
translations.idiomatic: During the attack on Jiqing, Guoxing was killed in battle, and Cheng succeeded to his command.

sentences.zh: 既而朝用請老，晟方從鄧愈克徽州，召還，襲父官。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chaoyong requested retirement; Cheng was just following Deng Yu in capturing Huizhou—recalled, he inherited his father's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyong later requested retirement, Cheng was with Deng Yu capturing Huizhou. Recalled from the campaign, he inherited his father's post.

sentences.zh: 累進都指揮同知，歷鎮江西、大同、陜西。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to regional military commissioner of the third rank, successively commanding at Jiangxi, Datong, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to regional military commissioner of the third rank and successively served as regional commander in Jiangxi, Datong, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 洪武十二年坐法降涼州衛指揮使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongwu, through violation of law he was demoted to garrison commander of Liangzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Hongwu he was demoted for an offense to garrison commander of Liangzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月討西番叛酋，至亦集乃路，擒元海道千戶也先帖木兒、國公吳把都剌赤等，俘獲萬八千人，送酋長京師，簡其精銳千人補卒伍，余悉放遣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he campaigned against the rebellious chieftains of the western barbarians; reaching Yijina'i Road, he captured the Yuan maritime-route chiliarch Esentemür, the state duke Wu Badur chi, and others, taking captive eighteen thousand persons; he sent the chieftains to the capital, selected one thousand elite men to fill the ranks, and released the rest entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he marched against rebel chieftains of the western tribes. Reaching Yijina'i Road, he captured the Yuan maritime-route chiliarch Esentemür, the state duke Wu Badur chi, and others—altogether eighteen thousand captives. He sent the chieftains to the capital, drafted one thousand of their best troops into the ranks, and released the remainder.

sentences.zh: 召還，復為都指揮，進右軍都督僉事，仍鎮涼州。

translations.literal: Recalled, he again became regional commander, advanced to assistant regional commander of the Rear Army, and still commanded at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was restored as regional commander, promoted to assistant regional commander of the Rear Army, and continued to hold command at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十四年充總兵官，與都督劉真討哈梅裏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he served as overall commander, together with Commissioner-in-Chief Liu Zhen campaigning against Hami.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he served as overall commander and, with Commissioner-in-Chief Liu Zhen, campaigned against Hami.

sentences.zh: 其地去肅州千餘里。

translations.literal: That place was more than a thousand li from Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hami lay more than a thousand li from Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 晟令軍中多具糧糗，倍道疾馳，乘夜至城下。

translations.literal: Cheng ordered the army to prepare much dried provisions, doubled the march speed at forced pace, and by night reached below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had the army carry abundant dry rations and forced a rapid march, reaching the city walls under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 質明，金鼓聲震地，闔城股栗，遂克之。

translations.literal: At dawn, drums and gongs shook the earth; the whole city trembled in fear, and they then captured it.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak, drums and gongs shook the earth; the entire city trembled with fear, and the place was taken.

sentences.zh: 擒其王子別兒怯帖木兒，及偽國公以下三十餘人，收其部落輜重以歸。

translations.literal: They captured its prince Bie'erqietemür and more than thirty persons including the false state duke downward; they gathered its tribal baggage and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Hami's prince Bie'erqietemür and more than thirty others down to the false state duke, then withdrew with the tribe's baggage train.

sentences.zh: 自是番戎慴服，兵威極於西域。

translations.literal: From this the frontier barbarians feared submission, and military awesomeness reached its peak in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the frontier peoples submitted in fear, and Ming military prestige reached its height in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 明年五月從藍玉征罕東，徇阿真川，土酋哈昝等遁去。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he followed Lan Yu in campaigning against Handong, marched along Azhen River, and the native chieftains Haza and others fled away.
translations.idiomatic: The following May he followed Lan Yu on the campaign against Handong, advancing along the Azhen River while native chieftains such as Haza fled.

sentences.zh: 師還，調中軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: The army returned; he was transferred to assistant regional commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was reassigned as assistant regional commander of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 二十八年六月，從總兵官周興出開原，至忽剌江。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year, he followed overall commander Zhou Xing out from Kaiyuan to Hula River.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year he joined overall commander Zhou Xing in marching from Kaiyuan to the Hula River.

sentences.zh: 部長西陽哈遁，追至甫答迷城，俘人畜而還。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Xiyangha fled; pursuing to Pudami City, they took captive people and livestock and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chief Xiyangha fled; Cheng pursued him to Pudami City, took captives and livestock, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年拜征南右副將軍，討廣西帡幪諸寨苗，擒斬七千餘人。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Right Vice General for the Southern Expedition, campaigning against the Miao of the various stockades at Pingmeng in Guangxi; captured and beheaded more than seven thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Right Vice General for the Southern Expedition and campaigned against Miao stockades at Pingmeng in Guangxi, capturing or killing more than seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 又明年，總羽林八衛兵討平五開、龍裏苗。

translations.literal: Again the next year, commanding the troops of the eight guards of the Palace Guard, he campaigned to pacify the Miao of Wukai and Longli.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he led the eight Palace Guard garrisons and pacified the Miao of Wukai and Longli.

sentences.zh: 三十一年出鎮開平，從燕王出塞，還城萬全諸衛。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he went out to command at Kaiping, followed the Prince of Yan beyond the frontier, and on return walled the various guards at Wanquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he took command at Kaiping, accompanied the Prince of Yan on a campaign beyond the frontier, and on the return fortified the garrisons at Wanquan.

sentences.zh: 建文改元，仍鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: When the Jianwen reign era began, he still commanded at Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen era began, he continued to hold command in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，入朝，進後軍左都督，拜平羌將軍，遣還鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzu ascended the throne, he entered court, was advanced to Left Regional Commander of the Rear Army, appointed General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and sent back to command.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Chengzu took the throne, he came to court, was promoted to Left Regional Commander of the Rear Army, appointed General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and sent back to his frontier command.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年招降把都帖木兒、倫都兒灰等部落五千人，獲馬駝牛羊萬六千。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle he induced the surrender of the tribes of Badutemür, Lundu'erhui, and others—five thousand persons—and obtained sixteen thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongle he induced five thousand tribesmen under Badutemür, Lundu'erhui, and others to submit, and seized sixteen thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 封西寧侯，祿千一百石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining, with an emolument of 1,100 shi, hereditary garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining with an annual stipend of 1,100 shi and the hereditary rank of garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 晟凡四鎮涼州，前後二十餘年，威信著絕域。

translations.literal: Cheng altogether four times commanded at Liangzhou; front and back more than twenty years, prestige and authority were renowned in the remote regions.
translations.idiomatic: In all Cheng held command at Liangzhou four times over more than twenty years, and his prestige reached the farthest frontiers.

sentences.zh: 帝以晟舊臣，有大將材，專任以邊事，所奏請輒報可。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Cheng was an old minister with great general's talent, specially entrusted him with frontier affairs; whatever he memorialized requesting was always approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, regarding Cheng as a veteran with true generalship, gave him exclusive charge of frontier affairs, and his proposals were invariably approved.

sentences.zh: 御史劾晟自專。

translations.literal: A censor impeached Cheng for acting on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: A censor impeached Cheng for acting autocratically.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「任人不專則不能成功，況大將統制一邊，寧能盡拘文法。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If one does not entrust a man with full authority, success cannot be achieved; moreover, when a great general commands a frontier, how can he be fully bound by written regulations?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "If one does not give an appointee full authority, nothing can be accomplished—and when a major general controls an entire frontier, how can he be shackled by every rule in the code?"

sentences.zh: 即敕晟以便宜從事。

translations.literal: He at once ordered Cheng to act at his discretion as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately authorized Cheng to act at his discretion as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 晟嘗請入朝。

translations.literal: Cheng once requested to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng once requested leave to come to court.

sentences.zh: 報曰：「西北邊務，一以委卿，非召命，毋輒來。」

translations.literal: The reply said: "Northwestern frontier affairs I entirely entrust to you; unless summoned, do not come on your own."
translations.idiomatic: The reply read: "Northwestern frontier affairs are entirely yours; unless you are summoned, do not come on your own."

sentences.zh: 尋命營河西牧地，及圖出塞方略。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to develop pasture lands west of the river and to map plans for campaigns beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to develop pasture lands west of the Yellow River and to draft plans for campaigns beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 會病卒，五年七月也。

translations.literal: He happened to die of illness—it was the seventh month of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell ill and died, in the seventh month of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 晟三子。

translations.literal: Cheng had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長瑄，建文中為府軍右衛指揮使，戰靈璧，先登，斬數級，力鬥死。

translations.literal: The eldest Xuan, during Jianwen's reign served as garrison commander of the Right Guard of the Palace Army; at the battle of Lingbi he was first to ascend, beheaded several heads, and died fighting with full strength.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Xuan, was garrison commander of the Right Guard of the Palace Army during the Jianwen reign. At Lingbi he was first over the wall, killed several enemies, and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 瑄弟琥，尚成祖女安成公主，得嗣侯，予世券。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Hu, married Emperor Chengzu's daughter Princess Ancheng, obtained succession to the marquisate, and was granted a patent of hereditary entitlement.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Hu married Emperor Chengzu's daughter, Princess Ancheng, succeeded to the marquisate, and received a patent of hereditary entitlement.

sentences.zh: 八年佩前將軍印，鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he wore the seal of the former general and commanded at Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he bore the former general's seal and held command in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十年與李彬捕叛酋老的罕，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, together with Li Bin, he captured the rebellious chieftain Laodehan; captives and beheadings were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he and Li Bin captured the rebel chieftain Laodehan, taking many prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 召還。

translations.literal: Recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年坐不敬奪爵，並削駙馬都尉官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, through disrespect he was stripped of the marquisate and also removed from the office of Commandant of Attendants-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi he was stripped of his title for disrespect and also lost his post as Commandant of Attendants-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 宣德中復都尉。

translations.literal: During Xuande the commandant post was restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign his commandant rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 琥既廢，弟瑛嗣。

translations.literal: Hu having been deposed, his younger brother Ying succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu's deposition, his younger brother Ying succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 瑛尚鹹寧公主。

translations.literal: Ying married Princess Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: Ying married Princess Xianning.

sentences.zh: 正統中，歷掌左軍前府事。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong, he successively managed the affairs of the Front Office of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign he successively directed affairs in the Front Office of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌也先入寇，瑛充總兵官，督大同守將朱冕、石亨等戰陽和，全軍敗沒，瑛及冕皆戰死。

translations.literal: When the Oirat leader Esen invaded, Ying served as overall commander, supervising the Datong garrison commanders Zhu Mian, Shi Heng, and others in battle at Yanghe; the whole army was defeated and destroyed, and both Ying and Mian died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen of the Oirats invaded, Ying served as overall commander, directing Datong garrison commanders Zhu Mian and Shi Heng in the battle at Yanghe. The entire force was destroyed, and both Ying and Mian were killed.

sentences.zh: 贈鄆國公，謚忠順。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Duke of Yun, posthumous title Zhongshun.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Yun with the posthumous title Loyal and Obedient.

sentences.zh: 子傑嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 景泰中典禁兵宿衛，以謹慎稱。

translations.literal: During Jingtai he managed the forbidden troops on palace guard duty, renowned for prudence.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign he commanded the palace guard, noted for his careful conduct.

sentences.zh: 卒，子誠嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Cheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On his death his son Cheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 署右府事，復佩平羌將軍印，鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: Acting in the affairs of the Right Office, he again wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang and commanded at Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He acted in the Right Office, again bore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and held command in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 誠有材武，嘗出獵至涼州，遇寇掠牛馬北去。

translations.literal: Cheng had talent and martial ability; once on a hunting outing he reached Liangzhou, encountered bandits plundering cattle and horses and going north.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was skilled in arms; once while hunting near Liangzhou he encountered raiders driving stolen cattle and horses northward.

sentences.zh: 誠三矢殪三人，寇驚散，盡驅所掠還。

translations.literal: Cheng with three arrows killed three men; the bandits startled and scattered, and he drove back all that had been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng killed three raiders with three arrows; the rest fled in panic, and he recovered all the stolen livestock.

sentences.zh: 九傳至孫裕德，死流寇難。

translations.literal: Through nine transmissions to grandson Yude, he died in the calamity of roaming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After nine generations the line reached his grandson Yude, who was killed in the roving-bandit upheavals.

sentences.zh: 薛祿，膠人。

translations.literal: Xue Lu, a man of Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Lu was a native of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 行六，軍中呼曰「薛六」。

translations.literal: Sixth in birth order, in the army they called him "Xue Six".
translations.idiomatic: The sixth son in his family, he was called "Xue Six" in the army.

sentences.zh: 既貴，乃更名「祿」。

translations.literal: Having become honored, he then changed his name to "Lu".
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to prominence, he adopted the name "Lu".

sentences.zh: 祿以卒伍從燕起兵，首奪九門。

translations.literal: Lu from the ranks followed the Prince of Yan in raising troops, first seizing the Nine Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Lu rose from the ranks to follow the Prince of Yan in rebellion and was first to seize the Nine Gates.

sentences.zh: 真定之戰，左副將軍李堅迎鬥。

translations.literal: At the battle of Zhending, Left Vice General Li Jian came out to engage in combat.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Zhending, Left Vice General Li Jian came out to give battle.

sentences.zh: 鋒始交，祿持槊刺堅墜馬，擒之。

translations.literal: The vanguards had just clashed when Lu, grasping a spear, stabbed Jian and made him fall from his horse, capturing him.
translations.idiomatic: As the vanguards clashed, Lu impaled Jian with a spear, knocked him from his horse, and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 擢指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Promoted to assistant garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從援永平，下大寧、富峪、會州、寬河。

translations.literal: He followed in relieving Yongping, and captured Daning, Fuyu, Huizhou, and Kuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Yongping and helped capture Daning, Fuyu, Huizhou, and Kuanhe.

sentences.zh: 還救北平，先驅敗南軍遊騎。

translations.literal: Returning to rescue Beiping, as vanguard he defeated the Southern Army's roaming cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to relieve Beiping, he led the vanguard and routed the enemy's scouting cavalry.

sentences.zh: 進指揮同知。

translations.literal: Advanced to garrison commander of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to garrison commander of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 攻大同，為先鋒。

translations.literal: Attacking Datong, he served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Datong he served as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 戰白溝河，追奔至濟南，遷指揮使。

translations.literal: Battling at Baigou River, pursuing the rout to Jinan, he was transferred to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: After fighting at the Baigou River and pursuing the rout as far as Jinan, he was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 戰東昌，以五十騎敗南兵數百。

translations.literal: Battling at Dongchang, with fifty horsemen he defeated several hundred Southern troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongchang he routed several hundred Southern troops with only fifty horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時成祖為盛庸所敗，還走北平。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Chengzu had been defeated by Sheng Yong and fled back toward Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Chengzu had been defeated by Sheng Yong and was retreating toward Beiping.

sentences.zh: 庸檄真定諸將屯威縣、深州，邀燕歸路。

translations.literal: Yong dispatched the generals of Zhending to encamp at Wei County and Shenzhou, intercepting the Yan army's return route.
translations.idiomatic: Yong ordered the Zhending generals to occupy Wei County and Shenzhou and cut off the Prince of Yan's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 祿皆擊走之。

translations.literal: Lu all struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Lu attacked and drove them off in every case.

sentences.zh: 戰滹沱河，右軍卻。

translations.literal: Battling at Hutuo River, the right wing fell back.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of the Hutuo River the right wing gave ground.

sentences.zh: 祿馳赴陣，出入數十戰，破之。

translations.literal: Lu galloped to the battle line, going in and out in several tens of engagements, and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu galloped to the front, fought through dozens of clashes, and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 追奔至夾河，斬馘無算。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout to Jiahe River, beheadings and ear-tokens were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rout to the Jiahe River and took an incalculable number of heads.

sentences.zh: 戰單家橋，為平安所執。

translations.literal: Battling at Danjia Bridge, he was captured by Ping An.
translations.idiomatic: At Danjia Bridge he was captured by Ping An.

sentences.zh: 奮脫縛，拔刀殺守卒，馳還復戰，大敗安軍。

translations.literal: Exerting himself he broke free of his bonds, drew his sword and killed the guarding soldiers, galloped back and again fought, greatly defeating An's army.
translations.idiomatic: He broke his bonds, killed the guards, galloped back into battle, and routed Ping An's forces.

sentences.zh: 掠順德、大名、彰德。

translations.literal: He raided Shunde, Daming, and Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Shunde, Daming, and Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 攻西水寨，生擒都指揮花英。

translations.literal: Attacking the Western Water Stockade, he captured alive regional commander Hua Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on the Western Water Stockade he took Regional Commander Hua Ying alive.

sentences.zh: 乘勝下東阿、東平、汶上，連戰淝河、小河、靈璧，功最。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he captured Dong'e, Dongping, and Wenshang; in continuous battles at Fei River, Xiao River, and Lingbi his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Following up his victory he took Dong'e, Dongping, and Wenshang, and in successive battles at the Fei River, Xiao River, and Lingbi his achievements ranked first.

sentences.zh: 入京師，擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: Entering the capital, he was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the capital he was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年進同知。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle he was advanced to third-rank commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongle he was promoted to regional commissioner of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 八年充驃騎將軍，從北征，進右都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as Flying Cavalry General, followed the northern expedition, and was advanced to Right Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as Flying Cavalry General on the northern expedition and was promoted to Right Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 十年上言：「自古用人，必資豫教。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle he memorialized: "From antiquity in employing men, one must rely on prior instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongle he memorialized: "Since antiquity, the use of men has depended on prior training.

sentences.zh: 今武臣子弟閑暇不教，恐緩急無可使者。」

translations.literal: Now the sons and younger brothers of military officials in leisure are not instructed—I fear that in urgent need there will be none who can be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Today the sons of military families are left idle without training; I fear that in an emergency there will be no one fit to serve."

sentences.zh: 帝韙其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 會四方送幼軍數萬至，悉隸祿操習之。

translations.literal: It happened that from the four directions several tens of thousands of young soldiers were sent—all were placed under Lu's command for drilling.
translations.idiomatic: When several tens of thousands of young recruits arrived from all quarters, they were all assigned to Lu for training.

sentences.zh: 十五年以行在後軍都督董營造。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, as touring Rear Army Regional Commander he supervised construction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he served as touring Rear Army Regional Commander supervising construction projects.

sentences.zh: 十八年十二月定都北京，授奉天靖難推誠宣力武臣，封陽武侯，祿千一百石。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighteenth year the capital was fixed at Beijing; he was granted the title Meritous Military Subject Who Supports Heaven, Settles Difficulties, Extends Sincerity, and Deploys Strength, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangwu, emolument 1,100 shi.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was established at Beijing in the twelfth month of the eighteenth year, he received the title Meritous Military Subject Who Supports Heaven, Settles Difficulties, Extends Sincerity, and Deploys Strength, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangwu with a stipend of 1,100 shi.

sentences.zh: 二十一年將右哨從北征。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he led the right wing and followed the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he led the right wing on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 還，討平長興盜。

translations.literal: Returning, he campaigned to pacify the bandits of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he suppressed banditry in Changxing.

sentences.zh: 二十二年再領右哨從北征。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he again led the right wing and followed the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he again led the right wing on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，命掌左府，加太子太保，予世券。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he was ordered to manage the Left Office, added as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and granted a patent of hereditary entitlement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was placed in charge of the Left Office, named Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and granted a patent of hereditary entitlement.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年充總兵官，備禦塞外。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he served as overall commander, preparing defense beyond the frontier pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi he served as overall commander defending the outer frontier.

sentences.zh: 尋以獲寇功，益祿五百石。

translations.literal: Soon, through merit in capturing bandits, his emolument was increased by 500 shi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received an additional stipend of 500 shi for capturing raiders.

sentences.zh: 是年頒諸將軍印於各邊鎮，祿佩鎮朔大將軍印，巡開平，至大同邊。

translations.literal: That year various general seals were issued to the frontier commands; Lu wore the seal of Great General Who Pacifies the North, patrolling Kaiping to the Datong frontier.
translations.idiomatic: That year frontier commanders received their general's seals; Lu bore the seal of Great General Who Pacifies the North and patrolled from Kaiping to the Datong frontier.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，召還，陳備邊五事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, he was recalled and set forth five matters for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Lu was recalled and presented five proposals for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 尋復遣巡邊。

translations.literal: Soon he was again dispatched to patrol the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out again to inspect the frontier.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年從征樂安，為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande he followed the campaign against Le'an as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande he served as vanguard in the campaign against Le'an.

sentences.zh: 高煦就擒，留祿與尚書張本鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Gao Xu having been captured, Lu was left together with Minister Zhang Ben to pacify and reassure the region.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Xu was captured, Lu and Minister Zhang Ben were left to pacify the area.

sentences.zh: 明年春，奉詔巡視畿南諸府城池，嚴戒軍士毋擾民，違者以軍法論。

translations.literal: In the spring of the next year, by imperial order he inspected the city walls of the various prefectures south of the capital region, strictly warning soldiers not to disturb the people—violators were prosecuted by military law.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was ordered to inspect the fortifications of prefectures south of the capital, with strict orders that troops must not harass civilians; violators would be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 是夏復佩大將軍印，北巡開平，還駐宣府。

translations.literal: That summer he again wore the great general's seal, patrolled north to Kaiping, and on return encamped at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he again bore the great general's seal, patrolled north to Kaiping, and on returning took up post at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 敵犯開平，無所得而退，去城三百餘里。

translations.literal: The enemy violated Kaiping, gained nothing and withdrew, three hundred-plus li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy raiders struck Kaiping, withdrew empty-handed, and were more than three hundred li from the city.

sentences.zh: 祿帥精兵晝伏夜行，三夕至。

translations.literal: Lu commanded elite troops, hiding by day and marching by night; in three nights he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Lu led elite troops by day marches and night marches, reaching the enemy in three nights.

sentences.zh: 縱輕騎蹂敵營，破之，大獲人畜。

translations.literal: He released light cavalry to trample the enemy camp, broke them, and greatly obtained people and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: He sent light cavalry to overrun the enemy camp, broke them, and captured large numbers of people and livestock.

sentences.zh: 師還，敵躡其後，復奮擊敗之，敵由是遠遁。

translations.literal: The army returned; the enemy followed on their rear, and he again exerted himself in striking and defeated them—thereby the enemy from this fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the enemy pursued from the rear; Lu turned and routed them, after which the raiders fled deep into the steppe.

sentences.zh: 召還。

translations.literal: Recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled.

sentences.zh: 三年從北征，破敵於寬河，留鎮薊州、永平。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the northern expedition, broke the enemy at Kuanhe River, and remained to command at Jizhou and Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined the northern expedition, defeated the enemy at the Kuanhe River, and remained to garrison Jizhou and Yongping.

sentences.zh: 復數佩鎮朔印，巡邊護餉，出開平、宣府間。

translations.literal: Again several times he wore the Pacify-the-North seal, patrolling the frontier and protecting grain supplies, going out between Kaiping and Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He several times again bore the Pacify-the-North seal, patrolling the frontier, escorting supplies, and operating between Kaiping and Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 五年遇敵於鳳凰嶺，斬獲多，加太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he encountered the enemy at Fenghuang Ridge; beheadings and captures were many, and he was added as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he met the enemy at Fenghuang Ridge, scored many kills and captures, and was named Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 上言永寧衛團山及雕鶚、赤城、雲州、獨石宜築城堡，便守禦。

translations.literal: He memorialized that at Tuanshan in Yongning Guard and at Diao'e, Chicheng, Yunzhou, and Dushi, fortresses should be built to facilitate defense.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that fortresses should be built at Tuanshan in Yongning Guard and at Diao'e, Chicheng, Yunzhou, and Dushi to strengthen the defenses.

sentences.zh: 詔發軍民三萬六千赴工，精騎一千五百護之，皆聽祿節制。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched 36,000 soldiers and civilians to the work; 1,500 elite horsemen to guard them—all were under Lu's command and control.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized 36,000 soldiers and civilians for the project, with 1,500 elite cavalry to protect them; all were placed under Lu's command.

sentences.zh: 臨行賜詩，以山甫、南仲為比。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he was granted a poem, compared to Shanfu and Nanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure the emperor presented him with a poem comparing him to the ancient ministers Shanfu and Nanzhong.

sentences.zh: 祿武人不知書，以問楊士奇。

translations.literal: Lu, a military man who did not know books, asked Yang Shiqi about it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, a soldier who was not literate, asked Yang Shiqi what the poem meant.

sentences.zh: 士奇曰：「上以古賢人待君也。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "The Emperor treats you as an ancient worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi replied: "The emperor is treating you as one of the sages of old."

sentences.zh: 祿拊心曰：「祿安敢望前賢，然敢不勉圖報上恩萬一。」

translations.literal: Lu clapped his chest and said: "How would Lu dare look to the former worthies—but how would I not strive to requite the Emperor's grace in the smallest measure?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu placed his hand on his heart and said: "How dare I compare myself to the great men of antiquity? Yet I shall strive with all my might to repay even a fraction of the emperor's kindness."

sentences.zh: 其年六月有疾，召還。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month he had illness and was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: That June he fell ill and was recalled.

sentences.zh: 逾月卒。

translations.literal: After a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a month later.

sentences.zh: 贈鄞國公，謚忠武。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Duke of Yin, posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Yin with the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 祿有勇而好謀，謀定後戰，戰必勝。

translations.literal: Lu had courage yet loved strategy; after planning was settled then he fought, and in fighting he invariably won.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was brave yet thoughtful: he planned first and fought afterward, and he invariably won.

sentences.zh: 善撫士卒，同甘苦，人樂為用。

translations.literal: Good at comforting soldiers, sharing bitterness and sweetness—men delighted in being employed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his soldiers well, sharing their hardships, and they served him willingly.

sentences.zh: 「靖難」諸功臣，張玉、朱能及祿三人為最，而祿逮事三朝，巋然為時宿將。

translations.literal: Among the "Pacify Difficulties" meritorious subjects, Zhang Yu, Zhu Neng, and Lu were the three foremost, yet Lu served three reigns and stood loftily as a veteran general of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Among the meritorious supporters of the "Pacification of Difficulties," Zhang Yu, Zhu Neng, and Lu ranked highest; Lu alone served three reigns and stood as the age's foremost veteran commander.

sentences.zh: 孫詵嗣。

translations.literal: His grandson Chuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Chuan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 至曾孫翰卒，無子，族人爭襲，久之不得請，田宅並入官，世絕者三十餘年。

translations.literal: When the great-grandson Han died without sons, clansmen disputed succession; for a long time they could not obtain approval; fields and residences all entered the government; the line was cut off for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: When his great-grandson Han died without an heir, clansmen fought over the title; for years no claimant was approved, the estates reverted to the state, and the line lapsed for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年乃復封翰族子鋹為侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, Han's clansman-son Qiang was at last again enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the fifth year of Wanli was Han's kinsman Qiang re-enfeoffed as marquis.

sentences.zh: 再傳至濂。

translations.literal: Through two more transmissions to Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later the line reached Lian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，京師陷，被害。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen, the capital fell, and he was harmed and killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, when the capital fell, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 永樂中從起兵北平，後積功至大將，封侯伯不以「靖難」功者，薛祿及郭義、金玉、劉榮、朱榮凡五人，而義、玉與祿同日封雲。

translations.literal: In Yongle, those who from raising troops at Beiping afterward accumulated merit to great general, enfeoffed as marquis or earl not on "Pacify Difficulties" merit—Xue Lu and Guo Yi, Jin Yu, Liu Rong, Zhu Rong—five persons in all; and Yi and Yu with Lu on the same day received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle, five men who had joined the Beiping rebellion and later rose to high command were enfeoffed as marquises or earls on grounds other than "Pacification of Difficulties" merit: Xue Lu, Guo Yi, Jin Yu, Liu Rong, and Zhu Rong; Guo Yi and Jin Yu received their titles on the same day as Lu.

sentences.zh: 郭義，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Guo Yi, a man of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi was a native of Jining.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，累功為燕山千戶。

translations.literal: During Hongwu, through accumulated merit he became chiliarch of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he rose through accumulated merit to chiliarch of Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 從成祖入京師，累遷左都督。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Chengzu in entering the capital, repeatedly transferred to Left Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Chengzu into the capital and was promoted step by step to Left Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年坐曠職謫交阯，立功，已而宥之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle, through neglect of duty he was demoted to Jiaozhi; he achieved merit, and thereafter was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongle he was banished to Jiaozhi for absenteeism; after distinguishing himself there he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 數從出塞，有功，封安陽侯，祿千一百石，亦授奉天靖難武臣號。

translations.literal: Several times he followed beyond the frontier, had merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang, emolument 1,100 shi, and also granted the title Meritous Military Subject Who Supports Heaven and Pacifies Difficulties.
translations.idiomatic: After several successful campaigns beyond the frontier he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang with a stipend of 1,100 shi and granted the title Meritous Military Subject Who Supports Heaven and Pacifies Difficulties.

sentences.zh: 時義在南京，疾革，聞命而卒。

translations.literal: At the time Yi was at Nanjing; severely ill, on hearing the order he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was in Nanjing at the time; gravely ill, he died upon receiving the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 金玉，江浦人。

translations.literal: Jin Yu, a man of Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yu was a native of Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 襲父官為羽林衛百戶，調燕山護衛。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's office as centurion of the Palace Guard, transferred to Yanshan Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post as centurion of the Palace Guard and was transferred to the Yanshan Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 從起兵有功，累遷河南都指揮使。

translations.literal: Following in raising troops he had merit, repeatedly transferred to Henan regional garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the rebellion and was promoted step by step to regional garrison commander of Henan.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年進都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle he was advanced to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongle he was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 八年充鷹揚將軍從北征。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as Soaring Hawk General and followed the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as Soaring Hawk General on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 師旋，為殿。

translations.literal: The army turned back; he served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he commanded the rearguard.

sentences.zh: 至長秀川，收敵所棄牛羊雜畜亙數十里。

translations.literal: Reaching Changxiu River, he gathered enemy-abandoned cattle, sheep, and miscellaneous livestock extending several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: At the Changxiu River he collected enemy livestock abandoned along a front several tens of li long—cattle, sheep, and other animals.

sentences.zh: 十四年討平山西妖賊劉子進。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he campaigned to pacify the sorcerous bandit Liu Zijin of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he suppressed the Shanxi sorcerer-rebel Liu Zijin.

sentences.zh: 論前後功，封惠安伯，祿九百石。

translations.literal: Assessing merit before and after, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huian, emolument 900 shi.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his cumulative service he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huian with a stipend of 900 shi.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year.

sentences.zh: 妾田氏自經以殉，贈淑人。

translations.literal: Concubine Tian hanged herself to follow him in death; granted the title Lady of Virtuous Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine Lady Tian hanged herself in fidelity; she was posthumously granted the title Lady of Virtuous Conduct.

sentences.zh: 劉榮，宿遷人。

translations.literal: Liu Rong, a man of Suqian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong was a native of Suqian.

sentences.zh: 初冒父名江。

translations.literal: Initially he falsely used his father's name Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He had initially taken his father's name, Jiang.

sentences.zh: 從魏國公徐達戰灰山、黑松林。

translations.literal: He followed Duke of Wei Xu Da in battling at Huishan and Heisonglin.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Duke of Wei Xu Da at the battles of Huishan and Heisonglin.

sentences.zh: 為總旗，給事燕邸。

translations.literal: Serving as chief squad leader, he attended to affairs at the Prince of Yan's residence.
translations.idiomatic: As chief squad leader he served in the household of the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 雄偉多智略，成祖深器之，授密雲衛百戶。

translations.literal: Imposing and with much strategizing, Emperor Chengzu deeply valued him and appointed him centurion of Miyun Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Imposing in bearing and adept in strategy, he won Emperor Chengzu's high regard and was appointed centurion of Miyun Guard.

sentences.zh: 從起兵為前鋒，屢立戰功。

translations.literal: Following in raising troops as vanguard, repeatedly establishing battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the rebellion as a vanguard and repeatedly distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 徇山東，與朱榮帥精騎三千，夜襲南軍於滑口，斬數千人，獲馬三千，擒都指揮唐禮等。

translations.literal: Marching through Shandong, together with Zhu Rong he commanded three thousand elite horsemen, by night attacking the Southern Army at Huakou; beheaded several thousand persons, obtained three thousand horses, captured regional commander Tang Li and others.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing into Shandong, he and Zhu Rong led three thousand elite cavalry in a night attack on Southern forces at Huakou, killing several thousand, seizing three thousand horses, and capturing Regional Commander Tang Li and others.

sentences.zh: 累授都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Repeatedly granted assistant regional military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to assistant regional military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戰滹沱河，奪浮橋，掠館陶、曹州，大獲。

translations.literal: Fought at the Hutuo River, seized the pontoon bridge, plundered Guantao and Caozhou, and gained greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at the Hutuo River, captured the pontoon bridge, raided Guantao and Caozhou, and won a great haul.

sentences.zh: 還軍救北平，敗平安軍於平村。

translations.literal: Returned the army to rescue Beiping, and defeated Ping'an's army at Ping Village.
translations.idiomatic: He marched back to relieve Beiping and routed Ping An's forces at Ping Village.

sentences.zh: 楊文以遼東兵圍永平，江往援，文引卻。

translations.literal: Yang Wen with Liaodong troops besieged Yongping; Jiang went to relieve it, and Wen withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wen besieged Yongping with Liaodong troops; Jiang marched to relieve the city, and Yang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 江聲言還北平，行二十餘里，卷甲夜入永平。

translations.literal: Jiang loudly declared he was returning to Beiping; after marching more than twenty li, he rolled up armor and by night entered Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang announced openly that he was returning to Beiping; after marching some twenty li, he doubled back under cover of night and re-entered Yongping.

sentences.zh: 文聞江去，復來攻。

translations.literal: Wen heard Jiang had gone, and again came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen heard that Jiang had departed, he returned to launch another attack.

sentences.zh: 江突出掩擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Jiang burst out in a surprise attack and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang sallied forth in a surprise attack and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 斬首數千，擒指揮王雄等七十一人。

translations.literal: Beheaded several thousand, and captured seventy-one including the commander Wang Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded several thousand enemies and took seventy-one prisoners, including the commander Wang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 遷都指揮使。

translations.literal: Was transferred to [the post of] Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commander.

sentences.zh: 從至淝河，與白義、王真以輕騎誘致平安，敗之。

translations.literal: Followed [the Prince] to the Fei River; with Bai Yi and Wang Zhen used light cavalry to lure and bring Ping'an, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince to the Fei River and, together with Bai Yi and Wang Zhen, used light cavalry to lure Ping An into battle and defeat him.

sentences.zh: 時南軍駐宿州，積糧為持久計。

translations.literal: At that time the Southern Army was stationed at Suzhou, storing grain for a prolonged campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the southern army was encamped at Suzhou, stockpiling provisions for a prolonged campaign.

sentences.zh: 成祖患之，議絕其餉道。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was troubled by this and discussed cutting off their supply route.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor was concerned by this and proposed cutting their supply lines.

sentences.zh: 命江將三千人往，趑趄不行。

translations.literal: Ordered Jiang to lead three thousand men to go; [he] hesitated and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jiang to lead three thousand men on the mission, but Jiang hesitated and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 成祖大怒，欲斬之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was greatly angered and wished to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and intended to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 諸將叩首請，乃免。

translations.literal: The generals kowtowed to plead, and then [he] was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The generals pleaded on their knees, and Jiang was spared.

sentences.zh: 渡江策功，以前罪不封，止授都督僉事。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed after crossing the river, because of the former offense he was not enfeoffed; only appointed Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were assessed after the crossing of the Yangzi, his earlier offense precluded enfeoffment; he was granted only the post of Assistant Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 遷中府右都督。

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Regional Commander of the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Regional Commander in the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年從北征，以遊擊將軍督前哨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle followed the northern expedition, as General of Mobile Operations supervising the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 8 he joined the northern campaign as General of Mobile Operations, commanding the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 乘夜據清水源，敗敵斡難河，復敗阿魯臺於靖虜鎮。

translations.literal: By night seized Qingshuiyuan, defeated the enemy at the Onon River, and again defeated Aruqtai at Jinglu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Qingshuiyuan by night, defeated the enemy on the Onon River, and routed Aruqtai again at Jinglu Fort.

sentences.zh: 師還為殿，即軍中進左都督，遣鎮遼東。

translations.literal: On the army's return served as rearguard; was promoted on the spot in the army to Left Regional Commander, and dispatched to garrison Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he served as rearguard, was promoted on the spot to Left Regional Commander, and posted to garrison Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 敵闌入殺官軍。

translations.literal: The enemy slipped in and killed government troops.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy slipped across the border and killed government troops.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命斬江，既而宥之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and ordered Jiang beheaded; afterward pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered Jiang's execution, but later pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 九年復鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the ninth year again garrisoned Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was again posted to garrison Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 十二年再從北征，仍為前鋒，將勁騎偵敵於飲馬河。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year again followed the northern expedition, again serving as vanguard, leading crack cavalry to scout the enemy at the Yinma River.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again joined the northern campaign as vanguard, leading elite cavalry to scout the enemy at the Yinma River.

sentences.zh: 見敵騎東走，追至康哈裏孩，擊斬數十人。

translations.literal: Saw enemy cavalry fleeing east, pursued to Kanghari, struck and beheaded several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing enemy cavalry fleeing east, he pursued them to Kanghari and killed several dozen.

sentences.zh: 復與大軍合擊馬哈木於忽失溫，下馬持短兵突陣，斬獲多，受上賞。

translations.literal: Again joined the main army in attacking Mahamu at Heshi Weng; dismounted, held short weapons and burst through the formation; killed and captured many, and received a superior reward.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoined the main army to attack Mahmud at Heshi Weng, dismounted to fight with side arms in a charge through the enemy lines, killed and captured many, and received a distinguished reward.

sentences.zh: 復充總兵官，鎮遼東。

translations.literal: Again appointed Commander-in-Chief, garrisoning Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed commander-in-chief to garrison Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 倭數寇海上，北抵遼，南訖浙、閩，瀕海郡邑多被害。

translations.literal: Wo pirates repeatedly raided at sea, reaching north to Liaodong and south to Zhejiang and Fujian; coastal commanderies and districts mostly suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese pirates repeatedly raided the coast from Liaodong in the north to Zhejiang and Fujian in the south, and many coastal districts suffered.

sentences.zh: 江度形勢，請於金線島西北望海堝築城堡，設烽堠，嚴兵以待。

translations.literal: Jiang assessed the situation and requested to build a castle at Wanghai Bao northwest of Jinxian Island, set up beacon towers, and strictly deploy troops to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Assessing the situation, Jiang requested permission to build a fort at Wanghai Bao northwest of Jinxian Island, establish beacon towers, and maintain a strong garrison on alert.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，瞭者言東南海島中舉火。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year, scouts reported fires raised on an island in the southeast sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year, scouts reported signal fires on a southeastern island.

sentences.zh: 江急引兵赴堝上。

translations.literal: Jiang urgently led troops to the bao.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang hastily led troops to the fort.

sentences.zh: 倭三十餘舟至，泊馬雄島，登岸奔望海堝。

translations.literal: More than thirty Wo ships arrived, anchored at Maxiong Island, landed and rushed toward Wanghai Bao.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty pirate ships arrived, anchored off Maxiong Island, landed, and rushed toward Wanghai Bao.

sentences.zh: 江依山設伏，別遣將斷其歸路，以步卒迎戰，佯卻。

translations.literal: Jiang set ambush relying on the hills, separately dispatched a general to cut off their return route, and with infantry met battle, feigning retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang laid ambush in the hills, sent another general to cut off the pirates' retreat, and engaged them with infantry in a feigned withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 賊入伏中，炮舉伏起，自辰至酉，大破賊。

translations.literal: The bandits entered the ambush; cannon fired and ambush rose; from the chen hour to the you hour, greatly defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates entered the trap, cannons fired and ambush parties sprang up; from morning until evening he routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 賊走櫻桃園空堡中，江開西壁縱之走。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to an empty fort at Cherry Orchard; Jiang opened the west wall and let them flee.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates fled into an abandoned fort at Yingtaoyuan; Jiang opened the west wall to let them escape.

sentences.zh: 復分兩路夾擊，盡覆之，斬首千餘級，生擒百三十人。

translations.literal: Again divided into two routes for pincer attack, completely overturned them; beheaded more than a thousand, captured alive one hundred thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He then split his forces in a two-pronged attack and destroyed them entirely, beheading more than a thousand and taking 130 prisoners.

sentences.zh: 自是倭大創，不敢復入遼東。

translations.literal: From this the Wo were greatly wounded and dared not again enter Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the pirates were so badly mauled that they dared not raid Liaodong again.

sentences.zh: 詔封廣寧伯，祿千二百石，予世券，始更名榮。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him as Baron of Guangning, salary 1,200 shi, granted hereditary certificate; then first renamed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangning with an income of 1,200 shi of grain, granted a hereditary certificate, and formally renamed Rong.

sentences.zh: 尋遣還鎮。

translations.literal: Soon dispatched to return to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 明年四月卒。

translations.literal: The next year in the fourth month died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following April.

sentences.zh: 榮為將，常為軍鋒，所向無堅陣。

translations.literal: Rong as general always served as army spearhead; wherever he went no strong formation stood.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander, Rong habitually led the vanguard and broke every strong enemy formation he faced.

sentences.zh: 馭士卒有紀律，恩信嚴明。

translations.literal: In controlling soldiers had discipline; kindness and trust were strict and clear.
translations.idiomatic: He governed his troops with discipline and combined strictness with kindness and trust.

sentences.zh: 諸款塞者，撫輯備至。

translations.literal: All who submitted at the frontier passes, he soothed and organized with utmost completeness.
translations.idiomatic: He treated all who submitted at the border passes with the utmost care and conciliation.

sentences.zh: 既卒，人鹹思之。

translations.literal: After he died, people all remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, he was fondly remembered by all.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚忠武。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Marquis; posthumous title Zhongwu (Loyal and Martial).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as a marquis with the posthumous name Zhongwu ("Loyal and Martial").

sentences.zh: 子湍嗣。

translations.literal: His son Tuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子，弟安嗣。

translations.literal: [Tuan] died without son; younger brother An succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuan died without an heir, his younger brother An succeeded.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年與郭登鎮大同。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, with Guo Deng garrisoned Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 14 he was posted with Guo Deng to garrison Datong.

sentences.zh: 也先擁英宗至城下，邀登出見，登不可。

translations.literal: Esen brought the Emperor Yingzong to below the walls and invited Deng to come out to see him; Deng would not.
translations.idiomatic: Esen brought the captive Emperor Yingzong to the city walls and invited Guo Deng to come out and meet him; Guo refused.

sentences.zh: 安出見，伏哭帝前。

translations.literal: An went out to see [him], prostrated and wept before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: An went out to meet the emperor, prostrated himself, and wept before him.

sentences.zh: 景帝降敕切責。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor issued an edict sharply rebuking [him].
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor issued an edict sharply rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 安馳至京師，言奉上皇命來告敵情，且言進己為侯。

translations.literal: An galloped to the capital, saying he came on the Former Emperor's order to report the enemy situation, and also said that [the Former Emperor] would advance himself to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: An rode in haste to the capital, claiming he had come on the former emperor's orders to report on the enemy—and that the former emperor had promised to promote him to marquis.

sentences.zh: 群臣交劾，下獄論死。

translations.literal: Ministers jointly impeached; imprisoned and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Officials jointly impeached him; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 會京師戒嚴，釋安充總兵官，陣東直門。

translations.literal: As the capital was on high alert, released An and appointed him Commander-in-Chief, arrayed at Dongzhimen.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was placed on high alert, he was released and appointed commander-in-chief, deployed at Dongzhimen.

sentences.zh: 寇退，進都督同知，守備白羊口，復伯爵。

translations.literal: When the invaders retreated, promoted to Vice Regional Commander, defended Baiyangkou, and restored the baronage.
translations.idiomatic: After the invaders withdrew, he was promoted to Vice Regional Commander, assigned to defend Baiyangkou, and restored to his baronial rank.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，予世侯，再益祿三百石。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong restored the throne, granted hereditary Marquis, and again added salary of three hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, An was granted a hereditary marquisate and an additional stipend of 300 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 曹欽反，安被創，加太子少傅。

translations.literal: When Cao Qin rebelled, An was wounded; added as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Cao Qin's rebellion, An was wounded and was appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 成化中卒。

translations.literal: Died in the Chenghua reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 贈嶧國公，謚忠僖。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Duke of Yi; posthumous title Zhongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Yi with the posthumous name Zhongxi ("Loyal and Diligent").

sentences.zh: 傳爵至明亡。

translations.literal: The transmitted title continued until the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: The hereditary title was passed down until the fall of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 朱榮，字仲華，沂人。

translations.literal: Zhu Rong, courtesy name Zhonghua, a man of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rong, styled Zhonghua, was a native of Yi.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年，以總旗從西平侯沐英征雲南。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu, as Chief Company Commander followed the Marquis of Xiping Mu Ying in the campaign against Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 14 he accompanied the Marquis of Xiping, Mu Ying, on the Yunnan campaign as a chief company commander.

sentences.zh: 累官副千戶。

translations.literal: By accumulated promotions reached Deputy Company Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to deputy company commander of a guard.

sentences.zh: 守大寧，降於成祖。

translations.literal: Defended Daning and surrendered to the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: While defending Daning, he surrendered to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 襲孫霖於滑口，圍定州，斷南軍餉道，大小二十餘戰，論功授都督僉事。

translations.literal: Raided Sun Lin at Huakou, besieged Dingzhou, cut off the Southern Army's supply route; in more than twenty battles large and small, on merit assessment was granted Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Sun Lin at Huakou, besieged Dingzhou, and severed the southern army's supply lines; after more than twenty engagements, he was rewarded with the post of Assistant Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年從新城侯張輔征交阯，破雞陵關，會沐晟於白鶴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle followed the Marquis of Xincheng Zhang Fu in the campaign against Jiaozhi, broke Jiling Pass, and joined Mu Sheng at Baihe.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 4 he joined the Marquis of Xincheng, Zhang Fu, on the campaign against Jiaozhi, captured Jiling Pass, and rendezvoused with Mu Sheng at Baihe.

sentences.zh: 輔等議於嘉林江上流濟師，遣榮陣下流十八里，日增其數以惑賊。

translations.literal: Fu and others planned to cross the army at the upper reaches of the Jialin River; sent Rong to array eighteen li downstream, daily increasing the numbers to confuse the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu and his colleagues planned to ferry the army across the upper Jialin River and sent Rong to deploy eighteen li downstream, increasing his reported numbers day by day to deceive the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又作舟筏為欲濟狀，以牽制之。

translations.literal: Also made boats and rafts showing an intention to cross, to tie down [the enemy].
translations.idiomatic: He also built boats and rafts to feign a crossing and tie down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊果分兵渡江登岸。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed divided troops, crossed the river and landed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy duly split their forces, crossed the river, and came ashore.

sentences.zh: 榮等奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Rong and others fought vigorously and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and his troops fought fiercely and routed them.

sentences.zh: 大軍進克多邦城，榮功為多。

translations.literal: The main army advanced and captured Duobang City; Rong's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: The main army then captured Duobang City, with Rong contributing the largest share of the victory.

sentences.zh: 帝以榮嘗怠事，師還論功，僅擢右都督，賜白金鈔幣。

translations.literal: The emperor because Rong had once been negligent in duty, when the army returned and merit was assessed, only promoted him to Right Regional Commander and bestowed white gold and paper currency.
translations.idiomatic: Because Rong had once been remiss in his duties, when rewards were assessed on the army's return he was promoted only to Right Regional Commander and given silver and banknotes.

sentences.zh: 七年復從輔討賊余黨，平之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year again followed Fu in suppressing the bandits' remnant factions and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he again joined Zhang Fu in suppressing the rebel remnants and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 明年督右掖，從征阿魯臺，與劉榮並進左都督。

translations.literal: The next year supervised the right flank, followed the campaign against Aruqtai; with Liu Rong both advanced to Left Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he commanded the right wing on the campaign against Aruqtai and was promoted alongside Liu Rong to Left Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 十二年復從北征，與榮俱為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year again followed the northern expedition; with Rong both served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again joined the northern campaign, serving alongside Liu Rong as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 其冬充總兵官，鎮大同。

translations.literal: That winter appointed Commander-in-Chief, garrisoning Datong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed commander-in-chief to garrison Datong.

sentences.zh: 修忙牛嶺、兔毛河、赤山、榆楊口、來勝諸城，寇不敢近。

translations.literal: Repaired the forts of Mangniu Ridge, Tumao River, Chishan, Yuyangkou, Laisheng, and others; invaders dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the forts at Mangniu Ridge, Tumao River, Chishan, Yuyangkou, Laisheng, and elsewhere, and the enemy no longer dared approach.

sentences.zh: 居三年，召還。

translations.literal: After residing three years, summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in post, he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 十八年，代劉榮鎮遼東。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, replaced Liu Rong in garrisoning Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he replaced Liu Rong as garrison commander of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十年復從北征，為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year again followed the northern expedition, serving as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he again joined the northern campaign as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 駐雕鶚诇寇，以五千騎視敵所向。

translations.literal: Stationed at Diaoge to reconnoiter the enemy, sent five thousand cavalry to observe where the enemy was heading.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Diaoge to scout the enemy and dispatched five thousand cavalry to track their movements.

sentences.zh: 大軍次玉沙泉。

translations.literal: The main army halted at Yusha Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The main army encamped at Yusha Spring.

sentences.zh: 榮帥銳士三百人，人三馬，賫二十日糧深入。

translations.literal: Rong led three hundred crack soldiers, each man with three horses, carrying twenty days' rations, penetrating deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Rong led three hundred elite troops, each with three horses and twenty days' provisions, on a deep raid.

sentences.zh: 敵已棄牛羊馬駝北走，悉收之，焚其輜重，移師破兀良哈。

translations.literal: The enemy had already abandoned cattle, sheep, horses, and camels and fled north; all were gathered; burned their baggage train; moved the army and broke the Uriyangkhad.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already abandoned their livestock and fled north; he collected it all, burned their baggage train, and moved on to defeat the Uriyangkhad.

sentences.zh: 師還，封武進伯，祿千二百石，仍鎮遼東。

translations.literal: On the army's return, enfeoffed as Baron of Wujin, salary 1,200 shi, still garrisoning Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wujin with an income of 1,200 shi of grain and continued to garrison Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十二年復從北征。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year again followed the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he again joined the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 已，還鎮。

translations.literal: Thereafter returned to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to his garrison post.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，佩征虜前將軍印，鎮如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, wore the seal of General Who Subdues the Barbarians, Vanguard, garrison as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 he was granted the seal of General Who Subdues the Barbarians, Vanguard, and continued in his garrison command.

sentences.zh: 其年七月卒於鎮。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month died at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post that July.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚忠靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Marquis; posthumous title Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as a marquis with the posthumous name Zhongjing ("Loyal and Tranquil").

sentences.zh: 子冕嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mian succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 以晉王濟熿新廢，命鎮山西，尋召還。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Jin Zhu Jihuang had just been deposed, ordered to garrison Shanxi; soon summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Jin, Zhu Jihuang, was recently deposed, Mian was ordered to garrison Shanxi but was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 六年命輸餉獨石，因巡其地。

translations.literal: In the sixth year ordered to transport provisions to Dushi, and thereby inspected that region.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was ordered to transport provisions to Dushi and took the opportunity to inspect the area.

sentences.zh: 正統四年，佩征西將軍印，鎮大同。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong, wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the West, garrisoning Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 4 he was granted the seal of General Who Pacifies the West and posted to garrison Datong.

sentences.zh: 十四年從北征，戰於陽和，死之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year followed the northern expedition, fought at Yanghe, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he joined the northern campaign, fought at Yanghe, and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 謚忠愨。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhongque.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Zhongque ("Loyal and Resolute").

sentences.zh: 子瑛嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ying succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 傳爵至明亡。

translations.literal: The transmitted title continued until the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: The hereditary title was passed down until the fall of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 費瓛，定遠人。

translations.literal: Fei Huan, a man of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Huan was a native of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖愚，洪武時為燕府左相，改授燕山中護衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yu, in the Hongwu reign served as Left Chancellor of the Prince of Yan's household, changed and appointed Commander of the Yanzhong Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu served in the Hongwu reign as Left Chancellor of the Prince of Yan's household and was later appointed commander of the Yanzhong Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 傳子肅。

translations.literal: Passed to son Su.
translations.idiomatic: The post passed to his son Su.

sentences.zh: 至瓛從成祖起兵有功，累進後軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: When [it came to] Huan, following the Prince of Yan in raising troops had merit; by accumulated promotions reached Assistant Regional Commander of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan joined the Prince of Yan's rebellion he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to Assistant Regional Commander of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年春，涼州衛千戶虎保、永昌衛千戶亦令真巴等叛，眾數千，屯據驛路。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year of Yongle, the Liangzhou Guard company commander Hubao, the Yongchang Guard company commander Yiling Zhenba, and others rebelled; their force numbered several thousand and encamped holding the post road.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Yongle 8, the company commanders Hubao of Liangzhou Guard and Yiling Zhenba of Yongchang Guard rebelled with several thousand men and seized control of the post road.

sentences.zh: 新附伯顏帖木兒等應之。

translations.literal: The newly submitted Bayan Temur and others responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: The recently submitted Bayan Temur and others joined them.

sentences.zh: 西鄙震動。

translations.literal: The western frontier was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 都指揮李智擊之不勝。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Li Zhi attacked them and did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Li Zhi attacked them but was defeated.

sentences.zh: 賊聲言攻永昌、涼州城。

translations.literal: The bandits loudly declared they would attack the cities of Yongchang and Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels announced their intention to attack the cities of Yongchang and Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 皇太子命瓛往討。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince ordered Huan to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince ordered Huan to go and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 至涼州，智及都指揮陳懷以師會，遂進兵鎮番。

translations.literal: Reached Liangzhou; Zhi and Regional Commander Chen Huai joined forces with the army, then advanced troops to Zhenfan.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Liangzhou, he joined forces with Li Zhi and Regional Commander Chen Huai and advanced on Zhenfan.

sentences.zh: 遇賊於雙城。

translations.literal: Met the bandits at Shuangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered the rebels at Shuangcheng.

sentences.zh: 瓛擊其左，懷等擊其右。

translations.literal: Huan struck their left; Huai and others struck their right.
translations.idiomatic: Huan attacked their left flank while Chen Huai and the others struck their right.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗走，斬首三百餘級。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly defeated and fled; beheaded more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed and fled, leaving more than three hundred dead.

sentences.zh: 追奔至黑魚海，獲賊千餘，馬駝牛羊十二萬。

translations.literal: Pursued the fleeing to Heiyu Sea, captured more than a thousand bandits, and horses, camels, cattle, and sheep numbering one hundred twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fugitives to Heiyu Sea, captured more than a thousand rebels, and seized 120,000 horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 虎保等遠遁。

translations.literal: Hubao and others fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Hubao and the other ringleaders fled into the distance.

sentences.zh: 乃班師。

translations.literal: Then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 十二年充總兵官，鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year appointed Commander-in-Chief, garrisoning Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed commander-in-chief to garrison Gansu.

sentences.zh: 瓛以肅州兵多糧少，脫有調發，猝難措置，請以臨鞏稅糧付近邊軍丁轉運。

translations.literal: Huan because Suzhou had many troops and little grain, should there be a mobilization it would be hard to arrange suddenly; requested that tax grain from Linqiong be given to nearby border soldiers for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Noting that Suzhou had many troops but little grain and that sudden mobilization would be hard to supply, Huan requested that tax grain from Linqiong be assigned to nearby border troops for transport.

sentences.zh: 又以涼州多閑田，請給軍屯墾。

translations.literal: Also because Liangzhou had much idle land, requested that it be given to troops for garrison farming and reclamation.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Liangzhou had much unused land and requested that it be allotted to troops for military colonization.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年予平羌將軍印。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi granted the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 he was granted the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，諸邊率用宦官協鎮，恣睢專軍務，瓛亦為所制。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign, the various frontiers generally used eunuchs to assist in garrisoning; they acted arbitrarily and monopolized military affairs, and Huan too was controlled by them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, eunuchs were routinely posted to assist frontier garrisons, where they acted arbitrarily and dominated military affairs; Huan too fell under their control.

sentences.zh: 仁宗知之，賜璽書責之曰：「爾以名臣後，受國重寄，乃俯首受制於人，豈大丈夫所為！

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor learned of this and bestowed an imperial letter reproaching him, saying: "You, as the descendant of a renowned minister, have received the state's heavy trust, yet bow your head and submit to being controlled by others—is this what a true man should do!
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor learned of this, he sent an imperial letter reproaching him: "You are the descendant of a renowned minister and have been entrusted with a weighty charge of state, yet you bow your head and submit to control by others—is this what a true man should do!

sentences.zh: 其痛自懲艾，圖後效。」

translations.literal: Severely chastise yourself and strive for future achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Chastise yourself severely and strive to redeem yourself hereafter."

sentences.zh: 瓛得書陳謝。

translations.literal: Huan received the letter and submitted a statement of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Huan received the letter and submitted a formal apology.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嗣位，進右府左都督。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor succeeded the throne, advanced to Left Regional Commander of the Right Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande Emperor succeeded to the throne, Huan was promoted to Left Regional Commander in the Right Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 元年七月入朝，封崇信伯，祿千一百石。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year entered court audience; enfeoffed as Baron of Chongxin, salary 1,100 shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year he came to court and was enfeoffed as Baron of Chongxin with an income of 1,100 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 從征高煦，次流河驛。

translations.literal: Followed the campaign against Gao Xu, halted at Liuhe Post.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Zhu Gaoxu and encamped at Liuhe Post.

sentences.zh: 帝念前鋒薛祿軍少，命瓛帥兵益之。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that the vanguard Xue Lu's army was few, ordered Huan to lead troops to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that the vanguard Xue Lu had too few troops, the emperor ordered Huan to lead reinforcements to his aid.

sentences.zh: 還，予世券，復鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: On return, granted hereditary certificate; again garrisoned Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was granted a hereditary certificate and resumed his garrison command in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二年，沙州衛賊屢劫撒馬兒罕及亦力把裏貢使，瓛討破之。

translations.literal: In the second year, bandits of Shazhou Guard repeatedly robbed the tribute envoys of Samarqand and Yili Bali; Huan suppressed and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, rebels from Shazhou Guard repeatedly robbed tribute envoys from Samarqand and Yili Bali; Huan defeated and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 明年卒於鎮。

translations.literal: The next year died at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post the following year.

sentences.zh: 瓛為人和易，善撫士。

translations.literal: Huan as a person was gentle and easygoing, good at soothing soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was affable by nature and skilled at winning over his troops.

sentences.zh: 在鎮十五年，境內寧謐。

translations.literal: At the garrison fifteen years; within the territory was peaceful and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: During fifteen years in command, the region under his charge remained peaceful.

sentences.zh: 子釗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 從征鄧茂七，還掌都督府。

translations.literal: Followed the campaign against Deng Maoqi; on return took charge of the Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Deng Maoqi and on his return took charge of the Regional Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 天順中，受武定侯郭英次孫昭賂，誣嫡孫昌不孝，欲奪其爵。

translations.literal: In the Tianshun reign, received bribes from Zhao, the second grandson of the Marquis of Wuding Guo Ying, falsely accused the legitimate grandson Chang of unfilial conduct, and wished to seize his title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshun reign he accepted bribes from Zhao, the second grandson of the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Ying, and falsely accused the legitimate heir Chang of unfilial conduct in an attempt to seize his title.

sentences.zh: 法司請逮治，詔解府事。
