translations.literal: The judicial offices requested arrest and punishment; an edict relieved him of commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial authorities requested his arrest and prosecution; an edict relieved him of his duties at the commission.

sentences.zh: 卒，子淮嗣爵。

translations.literal: Died; son Huai succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Huai succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 傳至明亡乃絕。

translations.literal: Transmitted until the Ming perished and then ended.
translations.idiomatic: The line continued until the fall of the Ming, when it died out.

sentences.zh: 譚廣，字仲宏，丹徒人。

translations.literal: Tan Guang, courtesy name Zhonghong, a man of Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Guang, styled Zhonghong, was a native of Dantu.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，起卒伍，從征金山，為燕山護衛百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, rose from the ranks, followed the campaign against Jinshan, and became a Company Commander of the Yanshan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Hongwu reign he rose from the ranks, joined the campaign against Jinshan, and became a company commander in the Yanshan Guard.

sentences.zh: 從成祖起兵，以百騎掠涿州，生得將校三十人。

translations.literal: Followed the Prince of Yan in raising troops; with one hundred cavalry raided Zhuozhou and captured alive thirty officers.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Prince of Yan's rebellion and, with a hundred cavalry, raided Zhuozhou and took thirty enemy officers alive.

sentences.zh: 戰白溝、真定、夾河鹹有功，屢遷指揮使，留守保定。

translations.literal: Fought at Baigou, Zhending, and Jiahe with merit; repeatedly promoted to Commander, and remained to guard Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with distinction at Baigou, Zhending, and Jiahe, rose through successive promotions to commander, and was left to garrison Baoding.

sentences.zh: 都督韓觀帥師十二萬來攻。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Han Guan led an army of one hundred twenty thousand to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Han Guan led an army of 120,000 against him.

sentences.zh: 廣以孤軍力拒四十餘日，伺間破走之。

translations.literal: Guang with an isolated army forcefully resisted more than forty days, waited for an opening and broke and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: With a lone garrison Guang held out for more than forty days and, seizing an opportunity, routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年進大寧都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle advanced to Assistant Commander of Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 9 he was promoted to Assistant Commander of Daning.

sentences.zh: 董建北京。

translations.literal: Supervised construction of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the construction of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 既而領神機營，從北征，充驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Thereafter commanded the Divine Engine Corps, followed the northern expedition, and served as General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded the Divine Engine Corps, joined the northern campaign, and served as General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十一年練軍山西。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year trained troops in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he trained troops in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年從征九龍口，為前鋒。

translations.literal: The next year followed the campaign at Jiulongkou, serving as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined the campaign at Jiulongkou as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 賊數萬憑岸，廣命挽強士射之。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of bandits relied on the bank; Guang ordered strong bowmen to shoot them.
translations.idiomatic: When tens of thousands of enemy troops held the riverbank, Guang ordered his strongest archers to shoot at them.

sentences.zh: 萬矢齊發，死者無算。

translations.literal: Ten thousand arrows released together; the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand arrows flew at once, and the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 乘勝夾擊，賊大敗。

translations.literal: Seizing victory, attacked from both sides; the bandits were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage with a pincer attack, he routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 論功，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: On merit assessment, advanced to Assistant Regional Commander.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Assistant Regional Commander.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，擢左都督，佩鎮朔將軍印，鎮宣府。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded the throne, promoted to Left Regional Commander, wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the North, garrisoning Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, Guang was promoted to Left Regional Commander, granted the seal of General Who Pacifies the North, and posted to garrison Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年，請軍衛如郡縣例，立風雲雷雨山川社稷壇。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande, requested that military guards, following the county and district precedent, establish altars to wind, cloud, thunder, rain, mountains, rivers, and the god of the soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 3 he requested that military guards, following the county and district precedent, establish altars to wind, cloud, thunder, rain, mountains, rivers, and the god of the soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 六年以宣府糧少，請如開平、獨石召商中鹽納粟，以足兵食。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because Xuanfu had little grain, requested that, as at Kaiping and Dushi, merchants be summoned to exchange salt for grain to fill out military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, noting the grain shortage at Xuanfu, he requested that merchants be invited—as at Kaiping and Dushi—to deliver grain in exchange for salt certificates in order to supply the troops.

sentences.zh: 俱從之。

translations.literal: Both were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Both requests were approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝從戶部議，令他衛軍戍宣府者，悉遣還屯種。

translations.literal: The next year, the emperor followed the Ministry of Revenue's proposal and ordered that troops from other guards garrisoning Xuanfu all be sent back to garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor adopted a proposal from the Ministry of Revenue and ordered troops from other guards stationed at Xuanfu to be sent back to their farms for garrison cultivation.

sentences.zh: 廣上言：「臣所守邊一千四百餘里，敵人窺伺，竊發無時。

translations.literal: Guang submitted a memorial, saying: "The border I guard extends over one thousand four hundred-odd li; enemies watch for openings and strike secretly without fixed times.
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted a memorial stating, "The frontier I defend stretches more than fourteen hundred li. Enemies watch for opportunities and can raid without warning at any time.

sentences.zh: 脫有警，征兵數百里外，勢豈能及？

translations.literal: If there is an alarm, troops are conscripted from several hundred li away—how could the force possibly arrive in time?
translations.idiomatic: If an emergency arises, troops must be levied from hundreds of li away. How could they possibly arrive in time?

sentences.zh: 屯種之議，臣愚未見其可。」

translations.literal: As for the proposal of garrison farming, this humble official's foolishness has not yet seen that it is feasible."
translations.idiomatic: As for the proposal to establish garrison farms, I fail to see how it could work."

sentences.zh: 帝以邊卒戍守有餘，但命永樂中調戍者勿遣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering that border troops had surplus for garrison duty, only ordered that those transferred for garrison during the Yongle reign not be redeployed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held that border garrisons already had sufficient troops for defense and ordered only that men transferred to frontier service during the Yongle reign not be sent away.

sentences.zh: 正統初，朝議以脫歡雖款塞，狡謀未可測，命廣及他鎮總兵官陳懷、李謙、王彧圖上方略。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong, the court discussed that although Toqtaq had submitted to the border, his crafty schemes could not be predicted, and ordered Guang and supreme commanders of other garrisons Chen Huai, Li Qian, and Wang Yu to draft strategy reports for the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengtong reign, the court judged that although Toqtaq had pledged allegiance at the frontier, his treacherous designs remained unpredictable. Guang and the supreme commanders of other garrisons—Chen Huai, Li Qian, and Wang Yu—were ordered to submit strategic plans to the throne.

sentences.zh: 廣等各上議，大要謂：「邊寇出沒不常，惟守禦為上策。

translations.literal: Guang and the others each submitted memorials; the main point was: "Border bandits appear and disappear without pattern; only defense is the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and the others each submitted recommendations, the gist of which was: "Frontier raiders come and go unpredictably; steadfast defense is the best strategy.

sentences.zh: 宜分兵扼要害，而間遣精稅巡塞外，遇敵則量力戰守，間諜以偵之，輕兵以躡之。

translations.literal: Troops should be divided to hold strategic points, while from time to time dispatching elite scouts to patrol beyond the passes; when encountering the enemy, fight or hold according to capacity; use spies to reconnoiter them, and light troops to pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: Troops should be divided to hold key positions, while elite detachments are periodically sent to patrol beyond the border. When the enemy is encountered, one should fight or hold according to circumstances; spies should be used for reconnaissance, and light forces to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 寇來無所得，去有所懼，則邊患可少弭。」

translations.literal: When bandits come and gain nothing, and when they leave they have fear, then border troubles can be somewhat allayed."
translations.idiomatic: If raiders gain nothing when they come and depart in fear, frontier troubles can be substantially reduced."

sentences.zh: 帝納其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted their words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted their recommendations.

sentences.zh: 六年十一月以禦敵功，封永寧伯，祿千二百石，仍鎮宣府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, for merits in repelling the enemy, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongning with a stipend of one thousand two hundred shi, and still commanded Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the sixth year, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongning with a stipend of 1,200 shi for his success in repelling the enemy, and continued to command at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 八年乞致仕。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he requested retirement from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 優詔不許。

translations.literal: A gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict graciously refused the request.

sentences.zh: 明年十月召還陛見。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year he was summoned back for an audience before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following year he was recalled to the capital for an audience.

sentences.zh: 帝憫其老，免常朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor, pitying his old age, exempted him from regular court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, taking pity on his advanced age, exempted him from regular court attendance.

sentences.zh: 是月卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: That month he died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same month at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 謚襄毅。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the title Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 廣長身多力，奮跡行伍至大將，大小百餘戰，未嘗挫衄。

translations.literal: Guang was tall in body and possessed great strength; he rose vigorously from the ranks to great general; in over one hundred battles large and small, he never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was tall and powerfully built. He rose from the ranks to become a senior general, fought in more than a hundred engagements large and small, and never suffered a setback.

sentences.zh: 在宣府二十年，修屯堡，嚴守備，增驛傳，又請頒給火器於各邊。

translations.literal: At Xuanfu for twenty years, he repaired garrison farms and forts, strictly maintained defenses, expanded courier stations, and also requested distributing firearms to the various frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: During twenty years at Xuanfu, he repaired garrison farms and fortifications, tightened frontier defenses, expanded courier stations, and also petitioned for firearms to be issued to the border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 將校失律，即奏請置罪，而撫士卒有恩。

translations.literal: When officers lost discipline, he immediately memorialized requesting punishment, yet in comforting soldiers he had kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When officers violated discipline, he immediately memorialized requesting their punishment, yet he treated the rank and file with kindness.

sentences.zh: 邊僥帖然，稱名將。

translations.literal: The border was nearly tranquil; he was called a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier remained largely peaceful, and he was acclaimed as an eminent general.

sentences.zh: 嘗逞憤杖殺都司經歷，又以私憾杖百戶，並為言官所劾。

translations.literal: Once in venting anger he beat and killed a dusi staff officer, and again out of private resentment beat a company commander; both were impeached by censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he beat to death a staff officer of the regional military commission in a fit of anger, and on another beat a company commander out of personal spite; in both cases he was impeached by censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 置不問，既卒，吏部言非世券，授其子序指揮使。

translations.literal: They were left unpunished; after his death the Ministry of Personnel said there was no hereditary certificate of nobility, and appointed his son Xu as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: No action was taken against him. After his death, the Ministry of Personnel noted that he had not held a hereditary patent of nobility and appointed his son Xu as a garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 陳懷，合肥人。

translations.literal: Chen Huai, a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huai was a native of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 襲父職為真定副千戶。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post as deputy company commander of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's position as deputy company commander at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，積功至都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongle, he accumulated merit to Vice Commissioner of the Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongle reign he accumulated merit until promoted to vice commissioner of the regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 從平安南，進都指揮使，蒞山西都司事。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Annam, was promoted to Regional Military Commissioner, and took charge of Shanxi Regional Military Commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Annam, was promoted to regional military commissioner, and assumed charge of the Shanxi regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 再從張輔擒安南賊簡定，從都督費瓛征涼州叛人虎保，皆有功。

translations.literal: Again he followed Zhang Fu in capturing the Annamese rebel Le Qui Ding, and followed Commissioner-in-chief Fei Yao in campaigning against the Liangzhou rebel Hu Bao; in all he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Zhang Fu in capturing the Annamese rebel Le Qui Ding and joined Commissioner-in-chief Fei Yao in suppressing the Liangzhou rebel Hu Bao, distinguishing himself in both campaigns.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，進都督同知。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded, he was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor acceded, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，代梁銘為總兵官，鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, he replaced Liang Ming as supreme commander and garrisoned Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande he replaced Liang Ming as supreme commander and took command at Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 時官軍征交阯者屢敗，詔發松潘軍援之，將士憚行。

translations.literal: At that time government troops campaigning in Jiaozhi repeatedly suffered defeat; an edict ordered dispatch of Songpan troops to reinforce them, and officers and soldiers dreaded going.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the government forces campaigning in Jiaozhi had suffered repeated defeats, and an edict ordered Songpan troops sent as reinforcements. The officers and men dreaded the assignment.

sentences.zh: 千戶錢宏與眾謀，詐言番叛，帥兵掠麥匝諸族。

translations.literal: Company commander Qian Hong conspired with the multitude, falsely claiming the tribes had rebelled, and led troops to plunder the Maiza and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Company commander Qian Hong conspired with his men, falsely reporting a tribal rebellion, and led troops to raid the Maiza and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 番人震恐，遂反。

translations.literal: The tribesmen were terrified and then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the tribesmen rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 殺指揮陳傑等，陷松潘、疊溪，圍威、茂諸州。

translations.literal: They killed Commander Chen Jie and others, captured Songpan and Diexi, and besieged Wei, Mao, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Commander Chen Jie and others, seized Songpan and Diexi, and besieged the prefectures of Wei, Mao, and others.

sentences.zh: 指揮吳玉、韓整、高隆相繼敗績，西鄙騷然。

translations.literal: Commanders Wu Yu, Han Zheng, and Gao Long suffered defeats in succession; the western frontier was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Wu Yu, Han Zheng, and Gao Long were defeated in succession, throwing the western frontier into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 詔遣鴻臚丞何敏、指揮吳瑋往招之，而命懷統劉昭、趙安、蔣貴帥師數萬隨其後。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Honglu Deputy Director He Min and Commander Wu Wei to go summon them, while ordering Huai to command Liu Zhao, Zhao An, and Jiang Gui to lead tens of thousands of troops to follow behind.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Honglu Deputy Director He Min and Commander Wu Wei to negotiate with the rebels, while Huai was ordered to command Liu Zhao, Zhao An, and Jiang Gui to lead an army of tens of thousands in their wake.

sentences.zh: 瑋等至，賊不順命。

translations.literal: When Wei and the others arrived, the rebels did not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Wei and his party arrived, the rebels refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 瑋與龍州知州薛繼賢擊賊，復松潘。

translations.literal: Wei joined with Longzhou Prefect Xue Jixian to attack the rebels and recovered Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wei joined Longzhou Prefect Xue Jixian in attacking the rebels and recovered Songpan.

sentences.zh: 比懷至，仍用瑋前鋒，遂復疊溪，降二十餘寨。

translations.literal: By the time Huai arrived, he still used Wei as vanguard, and thus recovered Diexi and reduced over twenty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Huai arrived, he kept Wu Wei in the vanguard, recovered Diexi, and brought more than twenty stockades to surrender.

sentences.zh: 招撫復業者萬二千二百餘戶，歸所掠軍民二千二百餘人，事遂定。

translations.literal: Over twelve thousand two hundred households were recruited and restored to their livelihoods, and over two thousand two hundred seized soldiers and civilians were returned; the affair was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: More than 12,200 households were restored to their livelihoods, and more than 2,200 captured soldiers and civilians were recovered. The affair was thus settled.

sentences.zh: 進左都督，厚賚金幣，而絀瑋功不錄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Commissioner-in-chief and richly rewarded with gold and silk, but Wu Wei's merit was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huai was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief and richly rewarded with gold and silk, but Wu Wei's achievements went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 懷留鎮四川。

translations.literal: Huai remained garrisoned in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huai remained in command in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 在鎮驕縱不法，干預民事，受賕庇罪人，侵奪屯田，笞辱僉事柴震等，數為言官所劾。

translations.literal: While in command he was arrogant and unrestrained in violation of law, interfered in civil affairs, accepted bribes to shield criminals, seized garrison farmland, and beat and humiliated Junior Commissioner Chai Zhen and others; he was repeatedly impeached by censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: While in command he was arrogant and lawless, meddled in civil affairs, accepted bribes to protect criminals, seized garrison farmland, and beat and humiliated officials such as Junior Commissioner Chai Zhen. He was repeatedly impeached by censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 帝降敕責讓，復以御史王禮彈章示之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent down an edict of reproof, and again showed him the memorial of impeachment by Censor Wang Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued an edict of rebuke and also showed him the impeachment memorial submitted by Censor Wang Li.

sentences.zh: 懷引罪。

translations.literal: Huai acknowledged guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Huai confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 置不問。

translations.literal: He was left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: No further action was taken against him.

sentences.zh: 六年，松潘勒都、北定諸族暨空郎、龍溪諸寨番復叛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Ledu, Beiding, and other tribes of Songpan together with the Konglang, Longxi, and other stockade tribes rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the Ledu and Beiding tribes of Songpan, together with the Konglang, Longxi, and other stockade tribes, rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 懷遣兵戰敗，指揮安寧等死者三百餘人。

translations.literal: Huai dispatched troops but was defeated; Commander An Ning and over three hundred others died.
translations.idiomatic: Huai sent troops but was defeated; Commander An Ning and more than three hundred others were killed.

sentences.zh: 懷乃親督兵深入，破革兒骨寨，進攻空郎乞兒洞。

translations.literal: Huai then personally supervised troops going deep in, broke Ge'ergu Stockade, and advanced to attack Konglang Qier Cave.
translations.idiomatic: Huai then personally led troops deep into enemy territory, captured Ge'ergu Stockade, and advanced to attack Konglang Qier Cave.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，斬首墜崖死者無算。

translations.literal: The rebels were defeated; those beheaded and who fell off cliffs died beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were defeated; those beheaded or who fell from cliffs were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 革兒骨賊復聚生苗邀戰。

translations.literal: The Ge'ergu rebels again gathered live Miao to intercept and give battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Ge'ergu rebels rallied living Miao tribesmen to intercept and engage them in battle.

sentences.zh: 擊破之，剿戮殆盡。

translations.literal: They were defeated and almost entirely exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: They were routed and nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 於是任昌、牛心諸寨番聞風乞降，群寇悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Renchang, Niuxin, and other stockade tribes submitted on hearing the news; all bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the tribes of Renchang, Niuxin, and other stockades submitted on hearing the news, and all the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 久之，巡按御史及按察使復奏：「懷僭侈逾分。

translations.literal: After some time, the touring censor and the provincial surveillance commissioner again memorialized: "Huai is extravagantly luxurious beyond his station.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, the touring censor and the provincial surveillance commissioner again memorialized: "Huai lives in extravagant luxury far beyond his rank.

sentences.zh: 每旦，令三司官分班立，有事跪白。

translations.literal: Each morning he had the officials of the three commissioner offices stand in separate ranks; if there were matters, they kneeled and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he had the officials of the three provincial commissions stand in separate ranks; when they had business to report, they knelt and addressed him.

sentences.zh: 懷中坐，稱旨行遣。

translations.literal: Huai sat in the middle; as he ordered, it was done.
translations.idiomatic: Huai sat in the center and issued orders as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 且日荒於酒，不飭邊備，致城寨失陷。」

translations.literal: Moreover he daily idled in wine, did not drill border defenses, causing fortresses and stockades to be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he daily indulged in wine, neglected frontier defenses, and allowed fortresses and stockades to fall."

sentences.zh: 宣宗怒，召懷還，命文武大臣鞫之，罪當斬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was angry, summoned Huai back, ordered civil and military grand ministers to interrogate him; the crime warranted decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor was enraged, recalled Huai, and ordered senior civil and military officials to try him. The offense warranted execution.

sentences.zh: 下都察院獄，宥死落職。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned in the Censorate prison; death was pardoned and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned in the Censorate jail; his death sentence was commuted and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 正統二年以原官鎮大同。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengtong, with his former rank he garrisoned Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengtong he was restored to his former rank and placed in command at Datong.

sentences.zh: 時北人來貢者日給廩餼，為軍民累。

translations.literal: At that time northerners coming to tribute were daily given provisions—a burden on soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the daily provisions given to tribute missions from the north had become a burden on soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 懷言於朝，得減省。

translations.literal: Huai spoke to the court and obtained reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Huai reported this to the court, and the allowances were reduced.

sentences.zh: 居二年，以老召還，命理中府事。

translations.literal: After two years in post, he was recalled due to old age and ordered to manage affairs at the Zhongfu.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in office he was recalled on account of age and ordered to manage affairs at the Zhongfu.

sentences.zh: 九年春，與中官但住出古北口，征兀良哈。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, together with eunuch Dan Zhu he went out through Gubeikou to campaign against the Uriangqai.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he marched out through Gubeikou with the eunuch Dan Zhu to campaign against the Uriangqai.

sentences.zh: 還與馬亮等同封，而懷得平鄉伯。

translations.literal: On return he was enfeoffed together with Ma Liang and others, and Huai received the title Baron of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was enfeoffed together with Ma Liang and others; Huai received the title Baron of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 十四年扈駕北征，死土木。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he accompanied the Emperor on the northern expedition and died at Tumu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he accompanied the Emperor on the northern expedition and died at Tumu.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚忠毅。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis; posthumous title: Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as a marquis and given the posthumous title Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 子輔乞襲爵，吏部言非世券，執不許。

translations.literal: His son Fu requested inheritance of the title; the Ministry of Personnel said there was no hereditary certificate and firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu petitioned to inherit the title, but the Ministry of Personnel argued that there was no hereditary patent and refused.

sentences.zh: 景帝以懷死事，許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingdi, because Huai died in service, permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingdi Emperor, in view of Huai's death in service, granted the request.

sentences.zh: 輔卒，子政請襲，吏部執如初，中旨許嗣。

translations.literal: When Fu died, his son Zheng requested inheritance; the Ministry held as before, but an imperial edict permitted succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died, his son Zheng petitioned to inherit the title; the Ministry of Personnel again refused, but an imperial edict permitted the succession.

sentences.zh: 政鎮兩廣久，自陳軍功，乞世券，吏部復執不可，詔予之。

translations.literal: Zheng long commanded the Two Guang; citing his military merit he requested a hereditary certificate; the Ministry again held it impossible, but an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had long commanded the Two Guang. Citing his military achievements, he requested a hereditary patent; the Ministry again refused, but an edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 政卒，子信嗣。

translations.literal: When Zheng died, his son Xin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng died, his son Xin succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 弘治中卒，無子，弟俊嗣指揮使。

translations.literal: He died in the Hongzhi reign without sons; his younger brother Jun succeeded as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Hongzhi reign without a son; his younger brother Jun succeeded as a garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 馬亮，淇人。

translations.literal: Ma Liang, a native of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Liang was a native of Qi.

sentences.zh: 以燕山衛卒從成祖起兵，累功至都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: As a soldier of Yanshan Guard he followed Chengzu in raising troops; he accumulated merit to Vice Commissioner of the Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: As a soldier of the Yanshan Guard he followed the Chengzu Emperor in raising troops and rose through merit to vice commissioner of the regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時官至左都督。

translations.literal: In the Xuande reign he reached the rank of Left Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign he rose to the rank of left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 兀良哈之役，偕中官劉永誠出劉家口，至黑山、大松林、流沙河諸處，遇賊勝之。

translations.literal: In the Uriangqai campaign, together with eunuch Liu Yongcheng he went out Liujiakou, reaching Heishan, Dasonglin, Liushahe, and other places; he encountered the enemy and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the Uriangqai, he marched out through Liujiakou with the eunuch Liu Yongcheng, reaching Heishan, Dasonglin, Liushahe, and other places, where he encountered the enemy and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 還封招遠伯。

translations.literal: On return he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 是役也，王振主之，故諸將功少率得封。

translations.literal: In that campaign Wang Zhen presided, so many generals' merits were meager yet mostly received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign Wang Zhen was in charge, so many generals with modest achievements nonetheless received enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 亮善騎射，每戰身先士卒，所向克捷，時稱驍將。

translations.literal: Liang excelled at mounted archery; in every battle he led from before the soldiers; wherever he went he achieved victory; at the time he was called a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was skilled in horsemanship and archery. In every battle he led from the front and won wherever he fought; at the time he was acclaimed as a fierce general.

sentences.zh: 為伯三年卒。

translations.literal: Three years after becoming baron he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died three years after receiving his baronial title.

sentences.zh: 謚榮毅。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Rongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the title Rongyi.

sentences.zh: 蔣貴，字大富，江都人。

translations.literal: Jiang Gui, courtesy name Dafu, a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gui, courtesy name Dafu, was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 以燕山衛卒從成祖起兵。

translations.literal: As a soldier of Yanshan Guard he followed Chengzu in raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: As a soldier of the Yanshan Guard he followed the Chengzu Emperor in raising troops.

sentences.zh: 雄偉多力，善騎射，積功至昌國衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: Stalwart and strong, skilled at mounted archery, he accumulated merit to Assistant Commander of Changguo Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Stalwart and powerfully built, and skilled in horsemanship and archery, he rose through merit to assistant commander of the Changguo Guard.

sentences.zh: 從大軍征交阯及沙漠，遷都指揮僉事，掌彭城衛事。

translations.literal: He followed the great army in campaigning against Jiaozhi and in the desert, was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Regional Military Commission, and managed Pengcheng Guard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main army in campaigns against Jiaozhi and into the desert, was transferred to vice commissioner of the regional military commission, and took charge of the Pengcheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，四川松潘諸番叛，充右參將，從總兵官陳懷討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, when the tribes of Songpan in Sichuan rebelled, he served as Right Assistant Regional Commander and followed supreme commander Chen Huai to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande, when the tribes of Songpan in Sichuan rebelled, he was appointed right assistant regional commander and followed supreme commander Chen Huai to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 募鄉導，絕險而進，薄其巢。

translations.literal: He recruited local guides, advanced by perilous paths, and closed on their nest.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited local guides, advanced by perilous routes, and closed in on the enemy stronghold.

sentences.zh: 一日十數戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: In one day over ten battles; he greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting more than ten engagements in a single day, he routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 進都指揮同知，鎮守密雲。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Regional Military Commissioner and garrisoned Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant regional military commissioner and stationed at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 七年復命為參將，佐懷鎮松潘。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again ordered as Assistant Regional Commander to assist Huai in commanding Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was again appointed assistant regional commander to assist Huai in commanding at Songpan.

sentences.zh: 明年進都督僉事，充副總兵，協方政鎮守。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief, appointed Deputy Supreme Commander, and cooperated with Fang Zheng in garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, appointed deputy supreme commander, and assisted Fang Zheng in frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 又明年，諸番復叛，政等分道進討。

translations.literal: Again the next year the tribes rebelled again; Zheng and others advanced by separate routes to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that the tribes rebelled again, and Fang Zheng and the others advanced by separate routes to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 貴督兵四千，攻破任昌大寨。

translations.literal: Gui supervised four thousand troops and broke Renchang Great Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Gui commanded four thousand troops and captured the great stockade at Renchang.

sentences.zh: 會都指揮趙得、宮聚兵以次討平龍溪等三十七寨，斬首一千七百級，投崖墜水死者無算。

translations.literal: Together with Regional Military Commissioners Zhao De and Gong Ju, troops in succession pacified Longxi and thirty-seven other stockades; beheaded one thousand seven hundred, and those who fell from cliffs or drowned died beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Together with regional military commissioners Zhao De and Gong Ju, his forces successively pacified Longxi and thirty-seven other stockades, taking 1,700 heads; those who fell from cliffs or drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，進都督同知，充總兵官，佩平蠻將軍印，代政鎮守。

translations.literal: Victory reported, he was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief, appointed Supreme Commander, wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and replaced Zheng in garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief, appointed supreme commander, invested with the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and replaced Fang Zheng in command.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，以所統皆極邊地，奏增軍士月糧。

translations.literal: When Yingzong acceded, because his command was all extreme frontier territory, he memorialized to increase soldiers' monthly grain ration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingzong Emperor acceded, noting that his command covered the most remote frontier regions, he memorialized for an increase in the soldiers' monthly grain rations.

sentences.zh: 正統元年召還，為右都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he was recalled and made Right Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong he was recalled to the capital and appointed right commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 阿臺寇甘、涼，邊將告急。

translations.literal: Atai raided Gan and Liang; frontier generals reported emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Atai raided Ganzhou and Liangzhou, and frontier generals sent urgent reports.

sentences.zh: 命佩平虜將軍印，帥師討之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and lead troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and lead an army against him.

sentences.zh: 賊犯莊浪，都指揮江源戰死，亡士卒百四十餘人。

translations.literal: Bandits invaded Zhuanglang; Regional Military Commissioner Jiang Yuan died in battle, and over one hundred forty soldiers were lost.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders invaded Zhuanglang; Regional Military Commissioner Jiang Yuan was killed in battle, and more than 140 soldiers were lost.

sentences.zh: 侍郎徐晞劾貴，朝議以貴方選軍甘州，勢不相及。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Xu Xi impeached Gui; court discussion held that Gui was just then selecting troops at Ganzhou and the force could not have reached there.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xu Xi impeached Jiang Gui, but the court held that Gui was then selecting troops at Ganzhou and could not have reached Zhuanglang in time.

sentences.zh: 而莊浪及晞所統，責晞委罪。

translations.literal: Yet as for Zhuanglang and those under Xi's command, Xi was held responsible for shifting blame.
translations.idiomatic: Responsibility for Zhuanglang and the forces under Xu's command was instead placed on Xu for shifting blame.

sentences.zh: 置貴不問。

translations.literal: Gui was left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gui was not punished.

sentences.zh: 明年春，諜報敵駐賀蘭山後。

translations.literal: The next spring, spies reported the enemy stationed behind Helanshan.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, intelligence reported that the enemy was encamped behind Helanshan.

sentences.zh: 詔大同總兵官方政、都指揮楊洪出大同迤西，貴與都督趙安出涼州塞會剿。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Datong supreme commander Fang Zheng and Regional Military Commissioner Yang Hong to go west from Datong, and Gui together with Commissioner-in-chief Zhao An to go out Liangzhou Pass for joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Datong supreme commander Fang Zheng and Regional Military Commissioner Yang Hong to march west from Datong, while Gui and Commissioner-in-chief Zhao An were to advance through the Liangzhou frontier pass for a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 貴至魚兒海子，都指揮安敬言前途無水草，引還。

translations.literal: Gui reached Yuerhai; Regional Military Commissioner An Jing said the road ahead had no water or grass, and led the force back.
translations.idiomatic: Gui reached Yuerhai, but Regional Military Commissioner An Jing reported that there was no water or pasture ahead and withdrew the force.

sentences.zh: 鎮守陜西都御史陳鎰言狀，尚書王驥出理邊務，斬敬，責貴立功。

translations.literal: Garrison Shaanxi Censor-in-chief Chen Yi reported the situation; Minister Wang Ji went out to manage frontier affairs, beheaded Jing, and ordered Gui to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Shaanxi Censor-in-chief Chen Yi reported what had happened; Minister Wang Ji went out to manage frontier affairs, executed An Jing, and ordered Gui to redeem himself through achievement.

sentences.zh: 貴感奮，會朵兒只伯懼罪，連遣使入貢，敵勢稍弱。

translations.literal: Gui was stirred to zeal; at the same time Doiratan feared punishment and repeatedly sent envoys to tribute; enemy strength weakened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Stirred to action, Gui took the field just as Doiratan, fearing punishment, repeatedly sent tribute missions, and enemy strength began to weaken.

sentences.zh: 貴帥輕騎敗之於狼山，追抵石城。

translations.literal: Gui led light cavalry and defeated them at Langshan, pursuing to Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gui led light cavalry to defeat them at Langshan and pursued them as far as Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 已，聞朵兒只伯依阿臺於兀魯乃地，貴將二千五百人為前鋒往襲。

translations.literal: Soon after, hearing that Doiratan relied on Atai at Wulunai land, Gui took two thousand five hundred men as vanguard to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, learning that Doiratan had joined Atai in the Wulunai region, Gui took 2,500 men as a vanguard to launch a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 副將李安沮之，貴拔劍厲聲叱安曰：「敢阻軍者死！」

translations.literal: Deputy general Li An discouraged him; Gui drew his sword and sternly shouted at An, saying: "Whoever dares obstruct the army dies!"
translations.idiomatic: Deputy general Li An tried to dissuade him, but Gui drew his sword and shouted at Li An: "Anyone who dares obstruct this army will die!"

sentences.zh: 遂出鎮夷。

translations.literal: Then he went out through Zhenyi.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched out through Zhenyi.

sentences.zh: 間道疾馳三日夜，抵其巢。

translations.literal: By a hidden route he galloped hard for three days and nights, reaching their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Taking a hidden route, he rode hard for three days and nights until he reached the enemy stronghold.

sentences.zh: 阿臺方牧馬，貴猝入馬群，令士卒以鞭擊弓韣驚馬，馬盡佚。

translations.literal: Atai was just herding horses; Gui suddenly entered among the horses, ordered soldiers to lash bow quivers with whips to startle the horses, and the horses all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Atai was just tending his horses when Gui suddenly rode into the herd and ordered his men to lash the horses' bow quivers with whips, stampeding them in all directions.

sentences.zh: 敵失馬，挽弓步鬥。

translations.literal: The enemy, having lost their horses, drew bows and fought on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Deprived of their horses, the enemy drew their bows and fought on foot.

sentences.zh: 貴縱騎蹂擊，指揮毛哈阿奮入其陣，大敗之。

translations.literal: Gui loosed cavalry to trample and strike; Commander Mao Ha'a charged vigorously into their formation and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui unleashed his cavalry in a crushing assault; Commander Mao Ha'a charged deep into the enemy formation and routed them.

sentences.zh: 復分軍為兩翼，別遣百騎乘高為疑兵，轉戰八十里。

translations.literal: Again he divided the army into two wings, separately sent one hundred cavalry on high ground as decoy troops, and fought turning over eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided his force into two wings, sent a separate detachment of one hundred cavalry to high ground as a decoy, and fought a running battle over eighty li.

sentences.zh: 會任禮亦追敵至黑泉，阿臺與朵兒只伯以數騎遠遁，西邊悉平。

translations.literal: When Ren Li also pursued the enemy to Heiquan, Atai and Doiratan fled far with a few horsemen; the western frontier was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Li also pursued the enemy to Heiquan, Atai and Doiratan fled far off with only a few horsemen, and the western frontier was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，王驥以捷聞，論功封定西伯，食祿一千二百石，給世券。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, Wang Ji reported victory; for merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Dingxi with a stipend of one thousand two hundred shi and granted a hereditary certificate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year, Wang Ji reported the victory; for his achievements Jiang Gui was enfeoffed as Baron of Dingxi with a stipend of 1,200 shi and granted a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年代任禮鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: The next year he replaced Ren Li in commanding Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he replaced Ren Li as commander in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 又明年冬，以征麓川蠻思任發，召還京。

translations.literal: Again the next year in winter, because of the campaign against the Luchuan barbarian Si Renfa, he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The winter of the year after that, he was recalled to the capital for the campaign against the Luchuan chieftain Si Renfa.

sentences.zh: 六年命佩平蠻將軍印，充總兵官，與王驥帥師抵金齒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, appointed Supreme Commander, and with Wang Ji led the army to Jinci.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was invested with the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, appointed supreme commander, and marched with Wang Ji to Jinci.

sentences.zh: 分路進搗麓川上江寨，破杉木籠山七寨及馬鞍山象陣，功皆第一。

translations.literal: Advancing by separate routes to strike Luchuan Upper Jiang Stockade, he broke Shanmuglongshan's seven stockades and the Ma'anshan elephant formation; in all merits he ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing by separate routes against the Upper Jiang stockade in Luchuan, he captured seven stockades at Shanmuglongshan and broke the elephant formation at Ma'anshan, ranking first in merit in each engagement.

sentences.zh: 事詳《王驥傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in the "Biography of Wang Ji."
translations.idiomatic: The details are given in the Biography of Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 明年，師還，進封侯，益祿三百石。

translations.literal: The next year the army returned; he was promoted to Marquis and given an increase of three hundred shi stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the army returned, he was promoted to marquis and his stipend was increased by 300 shi.

sentences.zh: 八年夏，復佩平蠻將軍印，與王驥討思任發子思機發，攻破其寨。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eighth year, again wearing the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, together with Wang Ji he attacked Si Renfa's son Si Jifa and broke his stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighth year, again invested with the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, he joined Wang Ji in attacking Si Renfa's son Si Jifa and captured his stockade.

sentences.zh: 明年，師還，賞賚甚渥，加歲祿五百石。

translations.literal: The next year the army returned; rewards were very generous, and five hundred shi was added to his annual stipend.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the army returned, he received lavish rewards and an additional annual stipend of 500 shi.

sentences.zh: 是役也，貴子雄乘敵敗，帥三十人深入。

translations.literal: In that campaign, Gui's son Xiong, while the enemy was defeated, led thirty men deep in.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign, Gui's son Xiong, taking advantage of the enemy's defeat, led thirty men deep into enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 敵扼其後，自刎沈於江。

translations.literal: The enemy blocked behind him; he cut his own throat and sank in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy cut off his retreat; he cut his own throat and sank in the river.

sentences.zh: 贈懷遠將軍、彭城衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as General of Huaiyuan and garrison commander of Pengcheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of Huaiyuan and garrison commander of the Pengcheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，貴卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, Gui died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year Jiang Gui died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈涇國公，謚武勇。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jing; posthumous title: Wuyong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jing and given the posthumous title Wuyong.

sentences.zh: 貴起卒伍，不識字，天性樸實。

translations.literal: Gui rose from the ranks, could not read; his nature was simple and honest.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gui rose from the ranks, was illiterate, and was by nature plain and honest.

sentences.zh: 忘己下人，能與士卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: He forgot himself to defer to others and could share hardship and comfort with soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He put others before himself and shared hardship and comfort with his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 出境討賊，衣糧器械常身自囊負，不役一人，臨陣輒身先之，以故所向有功。

translations.literal: Going beyond the border to attack bandits, clothes, food, weapons, and gear he always carried on his own back, not employing a single man; facing battle he always led from the front; for this reason wherever he went he had achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On expeditions beyond the border, he always carried his own clothing, provisions, weapons, and equipment without making a single man serve him, and always led the charge in battle; for this reason he succeeded wherever he fought.

sentences.zh: 子義，病不能嗣，以義子琬嗣侯。

translations.literal: His son Yi, ill, could not succeed; the adopted son Wan succeeded as Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was too ill to inherit the title, so his adopted son Wan succeeded as marquis.

sentences.zh: 天順末，佩平羌將軍印，總兵甘肅，築甘州沙河諸屯堡。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianshun, wearing the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang, he was supreme commander of Gansu and built Gansu Shahe and other garrison forts.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianshun reign he was invested with the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Qiang, commanded in Gansu, and built garrison forts at Gansu, Shahe, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 成化八年召還，協守南京，兼督操江。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua he was recalled, assisted in defending Nanjing, and concurrently supervised Jiangnan river defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chenghua he was recalled to assist in the defense of Nanjing and concurrently supervise the Yangzi river defenses.

sentences.zh: 十年入督十二團營，尋兼總神機營兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he entered to supervise the Twelve Tuan battalions, and soon also commanded Shenji battalion troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed to supervise the Twelve Tuan battalions and soon afterward also took command of the Shenji battalion.

sentences.zh: 上言：「太祖肇建南京，京城外復築土城以衛居民，誠萬世之業。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying: "Taizu when first establishing Nanjing, outside the capital also built an earthen wall to protect residents—truly an enterprise for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "When Taizu first established Nanjing, he also built an outer earthen wall to protect the populace—a truly enduring foundation for the ages.

sentences.zh: 今北京但有內城。

translations.literal: Now Beijing has only the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing today has only an inner city wall.

sentences.zh: 己巳之變，敵騎長驅直薄城下，可以為鑒。

translations.literal: In the Jisi disaster, enemy cavalry drove straight to beneath the walls—it can serve as a lesson.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jisi crisis, enemy cavalry rode straight to the foot of the walls—a lesson that should not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 今西北隅故址猶存。

translations.literal: Now the old foundations in the northwest corner still remain.
translations.idiomatic: The old foundations in the northwest corner still survive.

sentences.zh: 亟行勸募之令，濟以工罰，成功不難。」

translations.literal: Urgently issue an order of encouragement and recruitment, supplemented by labor fines—success is not difficult."
translations.idiomatic: If an urgent order is issued to encourage contributions and recruitment, supplemented by labor-service penalties, the work should not be difficult to complete."

sentences.zh: 又言：「大同、宣府諸塞下，腴田無慮數十萬，悉為豪右所占。

translations.literal: He also said: "Below the passes of Datong, Xuanfu, and other frontier defenses, fertile fields surely number in the hundreds of thousands—all occupied by powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Below the passes at Datong, Xuanfu, and other frontier garrisons, fertile land amounting to hundreds of thousands of mu has all been seized by powerful local families.

sentences.zh: 畿內八府，良田半屬勢要家。

translations.literal: Within the capital region's eight prefectures, half the good farmland belongs to influential and powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: In the eight prefectures of the metropolitan region, half the best farmland belongs to powerful and well-connected families.

sentences.zh: 細民失業。

translations.literal: Common people lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary people have lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 脫使邊關有警，內郡何資？

translations.literal: If the frontier passes have an alarm, with what will the interior commanderies be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: If the frontier posts come under threat, how will the interior commanderies be supplied?

sentences.zh: 運道或梗，京師安給？

translations.literal: If transport routes are blocked, how will the capital be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: If the transport routes are cut, how will the capital be provisioned?

sentences.zh: 請遣給事、御史按核塞下田，定其科額；

translations.literal: I request dispatching supervising secretaries and censors to examine and verify frontier fields below the passes and fix their tax quotas;
translations.idiomatic: I request that supervising secretaries and censors be sent to inspect frontier farmland below the passes and fix the tax quotas;

sentences.zh: 畿內民田，嚴戢豪右毋得侵奪。

translations.literal: As for civilian fields within the capital region, strictly restrain powerful families from seizing them.
translations.idiomatic: and that within the metropolitan region powerful families be strictly forbidden from seizing commoners' farmland.

sentences.zh: 庶兵民足食而內外有備。」

translations.literal: Then perhaps soldiers and people will have sufficient food and inner and outer will have preparedness."
translations.idiomatic: Then soldiers and civilians may have enough to eat, and both the interior and the frontier will be prepared."

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 雖不盡行，時論韙之。

translations.literal: Although not fully implemented, contemporary opinion approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Although not all of it was implemented, contemporary opinion approved his proposals.

sentences.zh: 十三年帥京軍防秋大同、宣府，陳機宜十餘事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he led capital troops for autumn defense of Datong and Xuanfu, and presented over ten strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he led capital troops on autumn defense duty at Datong and Xuanfu and submitted more than ten strategic recommendations.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were reported approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 十五年偕汪直按遼東邊事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, together with Wang Zhi he inspected Liaodong frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he joined Wang Zhi in inspecting frontier affairs in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二十年佩將軍印，出禦邊寇。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year [he] wore the general's seal, went out to repel border invaders.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was granted the general's seal and went out to repel border raiders.

sentences.zh: 寇退班師，累加太保兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the invaders retreated [he] withdrew the army; [he was] repeatedly promoted to Grand Guardian and concurrently Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew he returned with his troops and was successively promoted to Grand Guardian and Concurrent Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涼國公，謚敏毅。

translations.literal: [He] died; [was] posthumously ennobled Duke of Liang, posthumous title Minyi.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously granted the title Duke of Liang, with the posthumous epithet Minyi ("Diligent and Resolute").

sentences.zh: 子驥嗣，典京營兵。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded; [he] managed the capital garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded to the title and was placed in charge of the capital garrison forces.

sentences.zh: 弘治中充總兵官，歷鎮薊州、遼東、湖廣。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi era [he] served as regional commander, successively garrisoning Jizhou, Liaodong, and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he served as regional commander, holding commands at Jizhou, Liaodong, and Huguang in turn.

sentences.zh: 官中外二十年，家無余資。

translations.literal: [He] served at court and in the provinces for twenty years; the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He held office at court and abroad for twenty years yet left his family with no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 再傳至孫傅。

translations.literal: [It] passed down again to grandson Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed down to his grandson Fu in the third generation.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，累典軍府。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing era, [he] repeatedly managed military offices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign he repeatedly held senior military commands.

sentences.zh: 佩征蠻將軍印，鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: [He] wore the General for Pacifying the Barbarians seal, garrisoned the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was invested with the seal of General for the Pacification of the Man and stationed in the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 以平海賊及慶遠瑤功，加太子太保。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying sea pirates and the Yao of Qingyuan, [he was] promoted to Grand Guardian to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: For subduing sea pirates and the Yao of Qingyuan he was promoted to Grand Guardian to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 明亡，爵絕。

translations.literal: When Ming perished, the enfeoffment ended.
translations.idiomatic: With the fall of the Ming dynasty the hereditary title became extinct.

sentences.zh: 任禮，字尚義，臨漳人。

translations.literal: Ren Li, styled Shangyi, a native of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li, styled Shangyi, was a native of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 以燕山衛卒從成祖起兵，積功至山東都指揮使。

translations.literal: As a soldier of the Yanshan Guard he followed the Yongle Emperor in raising troops, accumulated merit until [reaching] Shandong regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a soldier in the Yanshan Guard, he followed the Yongle Emperor in rebellion and rose through merit to become regional commander of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十年擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yongle [he was] promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 20 he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從北征，前行偵敵，還受厚賞。

translations.literal: [He] followed the northern expedition, went ahead to reconnoiter the enemy, [and] upon return received generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern campaign he rode ahead to scout the enemy and was generously rewarded on his return.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，命掌廣西都司事。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended, [he was] ordered to administer Guangxi's regional command.
translations.idiomatic: Upon the Hongxi Emperor's accession he was appointed to manage the Guangxi regional military commission.

sentences.zh: 尋改遼東。

translations.literal: Soon [he was] transferred to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong established [the throne], [he was] promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande Emperor came to the throne he was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 從平樂安，又從征兀良哈，還為後拒。

translations.literal: [He] followed in pacifying Le'an, again followed in campaigning against Uriankhai, upon return served as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in suppressing Le'an and later joined the campaign against Uriankhai, serving as rear guard on the return march.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，進左都督。

translations.literal: When Yingzong established [the throne], [he was] promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengtong Emperor ascended he was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正統元年佩平羌將軍印，充左副總兵鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong [he] wore the General for Pacifying the Qiang seal, served as left deputy regional commander garrisoning Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 he was granted the seal of General for the Pacification of the Qiang and appointed left deputy regional commander at the Gansu garrison.

sentences.zh: 阿臺、朵兒只伯數犯肅州，璽書譙讓。

translations.literal: Atai and Dorzijibai repeatedly violated Suzhou; imperial edicts reprimanded [them].
translations.idiomatic: Atai and Dorzijibai repeatedly raided Suzhou, drawing reprimands via imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 二年復寇莊浪。

translations.literal: In the second year [they] again invaded Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: In the following year they raided Zhuanglang again.

sentences.zh: 都指揮魏榮擊卻之，擒朵兒只伯侄把禿孛羅。

translations.literal: Regional commander Wei Rong repelled them, captured Dorzijibai's nephew Batu Boluo.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Wei Rong drove them back and captured Dorzijibai's nephew Batu Boluo.

sentences.zh: 禮以聞。

translations.literal: Li reported it to [the throne].
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 三年與王驥、蔣貴出塞，敗朵兒只伯於石城。

translations.literal: In the third year together with Wang Ji and Jiang Gui [he] went beyond the border, defeated Dorzijibai at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined Wang Ji and Jiang Gui in a campaign beyond the frontier and defeated Dorzijibai at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 復分道至梧桐林、亦集乃，進至黑泉而還。

translations.literal: Again dividing forces [they] reached Wutong Forest and Ejinay, advanced to Heiquan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They then split their forces, reaching Wutong Forest and Ejinay, advanced as far as Heiquan, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 斬獲多，封寧遠伯，祿千二百石。

translations.literal: Many beheaded and captured; enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningyuan, stipend of twelve hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: With many enemies slain and captured, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ningyuan with a stipend of 1,200 shi.

sentences.zh: 明年還朝。

translations.literal: The next year [he] returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 又明年代貴鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: Again in the next year [he] replaced Gui garrisoning Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he replaced Jiang Gui as garrison commander in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 八年，赤斤蒙古衛都督且旺失加苦也先暴橫，欲移駐也洛卜剌。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Chijin Mongol Guard commissioner Qiwan Shijia, suffering from Esen's tyranny, wished to relocate and encamp at Yelubola.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Qiwan Shijia, commissioner of the Chijin Mongol Guard, chafing under Esen's oppression, sought permission to relocate his encampment to Yelubola.

sentences.zh: 禮以其地近肅州，執不許。

translations.literal: Li because that place was near Suzhou, obstinately did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li, finding the site too close to Suzhou, firmly refused to grant permission.

sentences.zh: 已，奏請建寺於其地。

translations.literal: Subsequently, [Qiwan Shijia] memorialized requesting to build a temple at that place.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwan Shijia then submitted a memorial requesting that a temple be built at the site.

sentences.zh: 禮復言許其建寺，彼必移居，遺後患，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Li again said that if one permitted them to build a temple, they would necessarily relocate, leaving later trouble; the matter was ultimately shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li argued that allowing the temple would inevitably lead them to settle there and create future problems; the proposal was ultimately abandoned.

sentences.zh: 時邊將家僮墾塞上田者，每頃輸糧十二石。

translations.literal: At that time border generals' household slaves who reclaimed frontier land paid twelve shi of grain per qing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, household retainers of frontier generals who reclaimed border lands were required to pay twelve shi of grain per qing.

sentences.zh: 禮連請於朝，得減四石。

translations.literal: Li repeatedly petitioned the court, obtaining a reduction of four shi.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li repeatedly petitioned the court and secured a reduction of four shi.

sentences.zh: 是時邊塞無警，禮與巡撫曹翼屯田積粟，繕甲訓兵，邊備甚固。

translations.literal: At this time the frontier had no alarms; Li together with Grand Coordinator Cao Yi carried out garrison farming to accumulate grain, repaired armor and trained troops; frontier defense was very solid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the frontier was quiet; Ren Li and Grand Coordinator Cao Yi organized garrison farming to stockpile grain, repaired arms, and drilled troops, making the border defenses very strong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，沙州衛都督喃哥兄弟爭，部眾離貳。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Shazhou Guard commissioner Nange and his brothers quarreled; the tribesmen were divided and disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Nange and his brothers of the Shazhou Guard fell into dispute, and their followers became divided and disaffected.

sentences.zh: 禮欲乘其饑窘，遷之內地。

translations.literal: Li wished to take advantage of their famine and distress, relocate them to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li sought to exploit their hunger and hardship by relocating them into the interior.

sentences.zh: 會喃哥亦請居肅州境內。

translations.literal: As it happened Nange also requested to dwell within Suzhou's borders.
translations.idiomatic: Coincidentally, Nange himself also requested to settle within Suzhou territory.

sentences.zh: 禮因遣都指揮毛哈剌往撫其眾，而親帥兵繼其後。

translations.literal: Li thereupon dispatched regional commander Mao Halao to go soothe their crowd, while personally leading troops to follow behind.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li therefore sent regional commander Mao Halao ahead to pacify Nange's followers, while he himself led troops in support.

sentences.zh: 比至，喃哥復持兩端。

translations.literal: When [they] arrived, Nange again wavered between two sides.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, however, Nange again hedged between the two options.

sentences.zh: 其部下欲奔瓦剌，禮進兵逼之，遂收其全部千二百餘人以還。

translations.literal: His subordinates wished to flee to the Oirats; Li advanced troops to press them, then gathered his entire following of over twelve hundred persons and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his followers attempted to flee to the Oirats, but Ren Li pressed forward with his army and brought back the entire group of more than 1,200 people.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, bestowed rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported to the throne, he was rewarded with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 時瓦剌也先方盛，封喃哥弟鎖南奔為祁王。

translations.literal: At that time the Oirat Esen was just flourishing; [Esen] enfeoffed Nange's younger brother Suonangben as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Esen of the Oirats was then at the height of his power and had enfeoffed Nange's younger brother Suonangben as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 禮以二寇合則勢益難制，遣人招之。

translations.literal: Li because if the two invaders joined forces their power would be still harder to control, sent men to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that an alliance between the two factions would make them harder to control, Ren Li sent envoys to win Suonangben over.

sentences.zh: 鎖南奔欲從未決，禮潛師直抵罕東，縶之以歸。

translations.literal: Suonangben wished to follow but had not decided; Li secretly moved troops directly reaching Handong, bound him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Suonangben was inclined to comply but hesitated; Ren Li secretly marched straight to Handong, seized him, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，賜禮鐵券，令世襲。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly rejoiced, bestowed on Li an iron certificate, ordering hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and granted Ren Li an iron certificate of investiture conferring hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 十四年，也先分道入寇，抵肅州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Esen divided forces to invade, reached Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Esen launched a multi-pronged invasion that reached Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 禮遣裨將禦之，再戰再敗，失士馬萬計。

translations.literal: Li dispatched subordinate generals to repel them; twice fought and twice defeated; lost soldiers and horses numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Li sent subordinate commanders to resist but suffered defeat in two engagements, losing tens of thousands of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 征還，以伯就第。

translations.literal: Recalled from campaign, as marquis retired to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from the frontier, he retired to his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，提督三千營，以老致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, supervised the Three Thousand Camp, due to age retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingtai reign he was appointed to supervise the Three Thousand Camp but retired due to old age.

sentences.zh: 久之，復起守備南京，入掌中府。

translations.literal: After a long while, again rose [from retirement] to defend Nanjing, entered to manage the Central Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled to serve as defender of Nanjing and given charge of the Central Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 禮自起卒伍，至大將，恪謹奉法。

translations.literal: Li from rising out of the ranks of soldiers to great general, scrupulously observed the law.
translations.idiomatic: From his beginnings as a common soldier Ren Li rose to become a senior commander, yet remained scrupulous and law-abiding throughout.

sentences.zh: 成化初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua [he] died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚僖武。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted marquis, posthumous title Xiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as marquis with the posthumous epithet Xiwu ("Reverent and Martial").

sentences.zh: 子壽嗣，總兵鎮陜西。

translations.literal: His son Shou succeeded, as regional commander garrisoned Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou succeeded to the title and served as regional commander of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 坐征滿四失律，宥死戍邊。

translations.literal: [He was] convicted for failure in discipline while campaigning against Man Si, pardoned from death to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for military misconduct during the campaign against Man Si and, though spared execution, was banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 子弘，予世指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Hong, granted hereditary regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong was granted the hereditary rank of regional commander.

sentences.zh: 趙安，狄道人。

translations.literal: Zhao An, a native of Didao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao An was a native of Didao.

sentences.zh: 從兄琦，土指揮同知，坐罪死，安謫戍甘州。

translations.literal: His cousin Qi, native assistant regional commander, convicted of crime and died; An was banished to garrison at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Qi, a native assistant regional commander, was executed for a crime, after which Zhao An was demoted and sent to serve at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年進馬，除臨洮百戶，使西域。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle [he] presented horses, was appointed Lintao company commander, sent on mission to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 he presented horses to the court, was appointed company commander of Lintao, and dispatched on a mission to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 從北征有功，累進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: [He] followed the northern expedition with merit, repeatedly promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself on the northern campaign and rose through successive promotions to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，松潘番叛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, Songpan tribes rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2 the tribes of Songpan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 充左參將，從總兵陳懷討平之，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: [He] served as left vice general, followed regional commander Chen Huai to pacify them, promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as left vice general, he joined regional commander Chen Huai in suppressing the rebellion and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時議討兀良哈，詔安與史昭統所部赴京師。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to campaign against Uriankhai; [the emperor] ordered An and Shi Zhao to lead their units to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When a campaign against Uriankhai was proposed, Zhao An and Shi Zhao were ordered to bring their units to the capital.

sentences.zh: 兀良哈旋來朝，命回原衛。

translations.literal: Uriankhai soon came to court, ordered to return to their original guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Uriankhai soon submitted tribute, they were ordered to return to their original guard posts.

sentences.zh: 使烏思藏，四年還。

translations.literal: [He was] sent to U-Tsang, returned in the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent on a mission to U-Tsang and returned after four years.

sentences.zh: 明年復以左參將從史昭討曲先，斬獲多。

translations.literal: The next year again as left vice general followed Shi Zhao to campaign against Quxian, many beheaded and captured.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again served as left vice general under Shi Zhao against Quxian, with numerous enemies slain and captured.

sentences.zh: 九年，中官宋成等使烏思藏，命安帥兵千五百人送之畢力術江。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, palace eunuch Song Cheng and others were sent to U-Tsang; [the emperor] ordered An to lead fifteen hundred troops to escort them to the Biliujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the eunuch Song Cheng was dispatched to U-Tsang; Zhao An was ordered to lead 1,500 troops to escort the mission to the Biliujiang River.

sentences.zh: 尋與侍郎徐晞出塞討阿臺、朵兒只伯，敗之。

translations.literal: Soon together with vice minister Xu Xi [he] went beyond the border to campaign against Atai and Dorzijibai, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Vice Minister Xu Xi in a campaign beyond the frontier against Atai and Dorzijibai and routed them.

sentences.zh: 正統元年進都督同知，充右副總兵官，協任禮鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong promoted to commissioner-in-chief, served as right deputy regional commander, assisted Ren Li garrisoning Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 he was promoted to commissioner-in-chief and appointed right deputy regional commander to assist Ren Li at the Gansu garrison.

sentences.zh: 明年與蔣貴出塞，剿寇無功。

translations.literal: The next year together with Jiang Gui [he] went beyond the border, cleared out invaders without merit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Jiang Gui in a raid beyond the frontier but achieved no success against the raiders.

sentences.zh: 三年，復與王驥、任禮、蔣貴分道進師，至刁力溝執右丞、達魯花赤等三十人。

translations.literal: In the third year, again with Wang Ji, Ren Li, and Jiang Gui divided forces advancing troops, reaching Diaoligou and seized right chancellor, darughachi and others, thirty persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again joined Wang Ji, Ren Li, and Jiang Gui in a multi-pronged advance, reaching Diaoligou and capturing thirty persons including the right chancellor and darughachi.

sentences.zh: 以功封會川伯，祿千石。

translations.literal: For merit enfeoffed as Marquis of Huichuan, stipend of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huichuan with a stipend of 1,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 明年移鎮涼州。

translations.literal: The next year transferred garrison to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to the Liangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 安家臨洮，姻黨廝養多為盜，副使陳斌以聞。

translations.literal: An's family was at Lintao; in-laws and attendants mostly became bandits; vice commissioner Chen Bin reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao An's family remained at Lintao, where his relatives and household retainers frequently turned to banditry; Vice Commissioner Chen Bin reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 在涼州又多招無賴為僮奴，擾民，復為御史孫毓所劾。

translations.literal: At Liangzhou moreover recruited ruffians as bond servants, harassed the people, again was impeached by censor Sun Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangzhou he further recruited ruffians as household bondsmen and harassed the populace, drawing impeachment from censor Sun Yu as well.

sentences.zh: 詔皆不問。

translations.literal: Imperial edict: all were not inquired into.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict ordered that all charges be dropped.

sentences.zh: 安勇敢有將略，與貴、禮並稱西邊良將。

translations.literal: An was brave and possessed generalship, together with Gui and Li was jointly called good generals of the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao An was courageous and skilled in command; together with Jiang Gui and Ren Li he was regarded as one of the finest frontier generals of the west.

sentences.zh: 九年十二月卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the ninth year [he] died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 子英為指揮使，立功，進都督同知。

translations.literal: His son Ying served as regional commander, [with] merit, promoted to commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying served as regional commander, distinguished himself in service, and was promoted to commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 趙輔，字良佐，鳳陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Fu, styled Liangzuo, a native of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fu, styled Liangzuo, was a native of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 襲職為濟寧衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Succeeded to the office as Jining Guard regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the post of regional commander of the Jining Guard.

sentences.zh: 景帝嗣位，尚書王直等以將才薦，擢署都指揮僉事，充左參將，守懷來。

translations.literal: When Jingdi succeeded to the throne, Minister Wang Zhi and others recommended him for generalship talent; promoted to acting vice regional commander, served as left vice general, defended Huailai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingtai Emperor succeeded to the throne, Minister Wang Zhi and others recommended him for his military talent; he was promoted to acting vice regional commander, appointed left vice general, and posted to defend Huailai.

sentences.zh: 天順初，征入右府蒞事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshun, summoned into the Right Military Commission to preside over affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianshun reign he was summoned to the Right Military Commission to take up duties.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，以中府都督同知拜征夷將軍，與韓雍討兩廣蠻，克大藤峽，還封武靖伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, as commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission appointed General for Subjugating the Yi, together with Han Yong campaigned against the Two Guangs barbarians, captured Dateng Gorge, upon return enfeoffed as Marquis of Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1, while serving as commissioner-in-chief of the Central Military Commission, he was appointed General for the Subjugation of the Yi and joined Han Yong in a campaign against the tribal peoples of the Two Guangs; after capturing Dateng Gorge he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wujing on his return.

sentences.zh: 已而蠻入潯州，言官交劾。

translations.literal: Before long the barbarians entered Xunzhou; censorial officials jointly impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the tribes raided Xunzhou, and censorial officials submitted a barrage of impeachments.

sentences.zh: 廣西巡按御史端宏謂：「賊流毒方甚，而輔妄言賊盡，冒封爵，不罪輔無以示戒。」

translations.literal: Guangxi touring censor Duan Hong said: "The bandits' ravages are at their height, yet Fu falsely claims the bandits are entirely eliminated and fraudulently received enfeoffment; if Fu is not punished there is no way to show admonition."
